children.text: daśakumāracaritam
children.translated_text: The Adventures of the Ten Princes (<s>Daśakumāracarita</s>)

children.text: pūrvapīṭhikā
children.translated_text: The Preliminary Section (<s>Pūrvapīṭhikā</s>)

children.text: prathamocchvāsaḥ
children.translated_text: First Chapter (<s>Prathamocchvāsa</s>)

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.1:
brahmāṇḍacchatradaṇḍaḥ śatadhṛtibhavanāmbhoruho nāladaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: The staff of the parasol of the cosmic egg (<s>brahmāṇḍa</s>), the stalk-staff of the lotus that is the abode of <s>Śatadhrṭi</s> (Brahmā),

children.text: kṣoṇīnaukūpadaṇḍaḥ kṣaradamarasaritpaṭṭikāketudaṇḍaḥ /
children.translated_text: the mast-staff of the ship that is the earth, the banner-staff of the ribbon that is the flowing celestial river,

children.text: jyotiścakrākṣadaṇḍastribhuvanavijayastambhadaṇḍo 'ṅghridaṇḍaḥ śreyastraivikramaste vitaratu vibudhadveṣiṇāṃ kāladaṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: the axle-staff of the wheel of luminaries, the pillar-staff of victory over the three worlds — may the foot-staff [of <s>Viṣṇu</s>] in the three strides (<s>Trivikrama</s>) bestow blessings upon you, [the foot that is] the staff of death for the enemies of the gods!

children.text: asti samastanagarīnikaṣāyamāṇā śaśvadagaṇyapaṇyavistāritamaṇigaṇādivastujātavyākhyātaratnākaramāhātmyā magadhadeśaśekharībhūtā puṣpapurī nāma nagarī // Dkc_1,1.1 //
children.translated_text: There is a city named <s>Puṣpapurī</s> (Flower City), the crest-jewel of the land of <s>Magadha</s>, whose greatness as a jewel-mine is proclaimed by the multitude of precious substances such as gems and the like — merchandise of incalculable variety, perpetually displayed — [a city that serves as] the touchstone for all other cities.

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.2:

tatra vīrabhaṭapaṭalottaraṅgaturaṅgakuñjaramakarabhīṣaṇasakalaripugaṇakaṭakajalanidhi mathanamandarāyamāṇasamuddaṇḍabhujadaṇḍaḥ, purandarapurāṅgaṇavanaviharaṇaparāyaṇataruṇagaṇikāgaṇajegīyamānayātimānayā śaradindukundaghanasāranīhārahāramṛṇālamarālasuragajanīrakṣīragiri śāṭṭahāsakailāsakāśanīkāśamūrtyā racitadigantarālapūrtyā kīrtyābhitaḥ surabhitaḥ svarlokaśikharoruruciraratnaratnākaravelāmekhalāyitadharaṇīramaṇīsaubhāgyabhogabhāgyavān, anavaratayāgadakṣiṇārakṣitaśiṣṭaviśiṣṭavidyāsambhārabhāsurabhūsuranikaraḥ, viracitārātisaṃtāpena pratāpena satatatulitaviyanmadhyahaṃsaḥ, rājahaṃso nāma ghanadarpakandarpasaundaryasodaryahṛdyaniravadyarūpo bhūpo babhūva // Dkc_1,1.2 //
children.translated_text: There, [lived a king] whose upraised arm was like Mount <s>Mandara</s> churning the ocean of the entire enemy army — terrifying with its horses, elephants, and camels, surging forth in waves of battalions of valiant warriors; who was perfumed on all sides by a fame whose glory was fashioned to fill the spaces between the quarters — [a fame] celebrated in song by the troupes of young courtesans devoted to pleasure-excursions in the gardens of the city of <s>Purandara</s> (Indra), [a fame] whose beauty resembled the autumn moon, jasmine, dense camphor-essence, mist, garlands, lotus-stalks, swans, the celestial elephant's ichor, milk, the mountain of silver (<s>Kailāsa</s>), the laughter of cowrie shells, and the radiance of the sky; who possessed the fortune of enjoying the beauty of the bride that is the Earth, [the Earth] garlanded with the shore of the jewel-ocean, exceedingly beautiful like the peak of the celestial world; who was [surrounded by] a brilliant host of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, resplendent with the accumulation of eminent and distinguished learning protected by the rewards of unceasing sacrifices; whose valor — inflicting torment upon his foes — was like a swan constantly weighed in the middle of the sky. A king named <s>Rājahaṃsa</s> (Royal Swan) came to be, of faultless and delightful form, rivaling in beauty the handsomeness of the god of love.

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.3:
tasya vasumatī nāma sumatī līlāvatīkulaśekharamaṇī ramaṇī babhūva // Dkc_1,1.3 //
children.translated_text: His queen was named <s>Vasumatī</s> — wise, the crest-jewel of the lineage of <s>Līlāvatī</s>, a charming woman.

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.4:

roṣarūkṣeṇa niṭilākṣeṇa bhasmīkṛtacetane makaraketane tadā bhayenānavadyā vaniteti matvā tasya rolambāvalī keśajālam, premākaro rajanīkaro vijitāravindavadanam, jayadhvajāyamāno mīno jāyāyuto 'kṣiyugalam, sakalasainikāṅgavīro malayasamīro niḥśvāsaḥ, pathikahṛddalanakaravālaḥ pravālaścādhārabimbam, jayaśaṅkho bandhurā lāvaṇyadharā kandharā, pūrṇakumbhau cakravākānukārau payodharau;jyāyamāne mārdavāsamāne bilasate ca bāhūr, iṣadutphullalīlāvataṃsakahlārakorakau gaṅgāvartasanābhirnābhiḥ, dūrīkṛtayogimanoratho jaitraratho 'tighanaṃ jaghanam, jayastambhabhūte saundaryabhūte vighnitayatijanārambhe rambhe coruyugam, ātapatrasahasrapatraṃ pādadvayam astrabhūtāni prasūnāni tānītarāṇyaṅgāni ca samabhūvanniva // Dkc_1,1.4 //
children.translated_text: When <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of Love) was reduced to ashes by the wrathful third eye [of <s>Śiva</s>] on [his] forehead, then, thinking 'this blameless woman [shall be my refuge],' out of fear — her mass of hair became his swarm of bees, the moon (the source of love) became her face that surpassed the lotus, the fish that serves as his victory-banner became the pair of her eyes united [with beauty], the <s>Malaya</s> breeze — hero of all the army's limbs — became her sighs, coral — the sword that pierces the hearts of travelers — became her lower lip, the conch of victory became her lovely neck that bore the river of grace, the two full pitchers (and <s>cakravāka</s>-like pair) became her breasts; her arms that surpassed [even] the most tender [things] shone forth, her navel was like a whirlpool of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> with slightly blossoming lotus buds as earring-ornaments, her buttocks — exceedingly dense — were a triumphal chariot that surpassed the desires of yogins, her pair of thighs — obstructing the endeavors of ascetics — were like [twin] <s>Rambhās</s> (plantain trees / celestial nymphs), [set upon] the pillar of beauty, her two feet were parasols of a thousand petals — and her other limbs too became, as it were, the weapons and flowers [of the Love-god].

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.5:
vijitāmarapure puṣpapure nivasatā sānantabhogalālitā vasumatī vasumatīva magadharājena yathāsukhamanvabhāvi // Dkc_1,1.5 //
children.translated_text: Dwelling in <s>Puṣpapura</s>, which surpassed the city of the gods, the king of <s>Magadha</s> enjoyed <s>Vasumatī</s> at his pleasure, as though she were the Earth herself, cherished with infinite luxury.

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.6:
tasya rājñaḥ paramavidheyā dharmapālapadmodbhavasitavarmanāmadheyā dhīradhiṣaṇāvadhīritavibudhācāryavicāryakāryasāhityāḥ kulāmātyāstrayo 'bhūvan // Dkc_1,1.6 //
children.translated_text: That king had three supremely obedient chief ministers named <s>Dharmapāla</s>, <s>Padmodbhava</s>, and <s>Sitavarman</s>, whose firm intellects surpassed even the preceptor of the gods in deliberation on affairs of state.

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.7:
teṣāṃ sitavarmaṇaḥ sumatī-satyavarmāṇau, dharmapālasya sumantra-sumitra-kāmapālāḥ padmodbhavasya suśruta-ratnodbhavāviti tanayāḥ samabhūvan // Dkc_1,1.7 //
children.translated_text: Of those, <s>Sitavarman</s>'s sons were <s>Sumatī</s> and <s>Satyavarmā</s>; <s>Dharmapāla</s>'s were <s>Sumantra</s>, <s>Sumitra</s>, and <s>Kāmapāla</s>; and <s>Padmodbhava</s>'s were <s>Suśruta</s> and <s>Ratnodbhava</s>.

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.8:
teṣu dharmaśīlaḥ satyavarmā saṃsārāsāratāṃ buddhvā tīrthayātrābhilāṣī deśāntaramagamat // Dkc_1,1.8 //
children.translated_text: <s>Satyavarmā</s>, who was righteous by nature, having realized the futility of worldly existence, desirous of pilgrimage, departed to another land.

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.9:
viṭanaṭavāranārīparāyaṇo durvinītaḥ kāmapālo janakāgrajanmanoḥ śāsanamatikramya bhuvaṃ babhrāma // Dkc_1,1.9 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kāmapāla</s>, ill-bred, devoted to rogues, actors, and courtesans, transgressing the authority of his father and elder brother, wandered about the earth.

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.10:
ratnodbhavo 'pi vāṇijyanipuṇatayā pārāvārataraṇamakarot // Dkc_1,1.10 //
children.translated_text: <s>Ratnodbhava</s> too, by virtue of his skill in commerce, undertook the crossing of the ocean.

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.11:
itare mantrisūnavaḥ purandarapurātithiṣu pitṛṣu yathāpūrvamanvatiṣṭhan // Dkc_1,1.11 //
children.translated_text: The remaining sons of the ministers, when their fathers had become guests of <s>Purandara</s>'s city [i.e., had died], continued as before [in their duties].

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.12:

tataḥ kadācinnānāvidhamahadāyudhanaipuṇyaracitāgaṇyajanyarājanyamaulipālinihi taniśitasāyako magadhanāthako mālaveśvaraṃ pratyagrasaṅgrāmaghasmaraṃ samutkaṭamānasāraṃ mānasāraṃ prati sahelaṃ nyakkṛtajaladhinirghoṣāhaṅkāreṇa bherījhaṅkāreṇa haṭhikākarṇanākrāntabhayacaṇḍimānaṃ digdantāvalavalayaṃ vighūrṇannijabharanamanmedinībhareṇākrāntabhujagarājamastakabalena caturaṅgabalena saṃyutaḥ saṅgrāmābhilāṣeṇa roṣeṇa mahatāviṣṭo niryayau // Dkc_1,1.12 //
children.translated_text: Then once, the lord of <s>Magadha</s>, whose arrows were sharpened, whose countless battle-honors were fashioned through his mastery of various great weapons — [he who was] like a <s>Mandara</s> mountain churning the ocean of the armies of all enemy kings — set forth with a vast fourfold army whose weight caused the earth to bow, as if pressing upon the head of the lord of serpents, accompanied by the thunderous beating of war-drums that contemptuously drowned out the roar of the ocean, with an arrogance that intimidated the guardian elephants of the quarters — set forth, filled with great anger, with a desire for battle, against <s>Mānasāra</s>, the lord of <s>Mālava</s>, whose pride was exceedingly fierce, who devoured [opponents] in fresh combat.

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.13:
mālavanātho 'pyanekānekayūthapasanātho vigrahaḥ savigraha iva sāgraho 'bhimukhībhūya bhūyo nirjagāma // Dkc_1,1.13 //
children.translated_text: The lord of <s>Mālava</s> too, accompanied by many, many commanders of elephant-divisions — [he who was] like battle incarnate, armed and aggressive — came forth to face [the enemy].

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.14:

tayoratha rathaturagakhurakṣuṇṇakṣoṇīsamudbhūte karighaṭākaṭasravanmadadhārādhautamūle navyavallabhavaraṇāgatadivyakanyājanajavanikāpaṭamaṇḍapa iva viyattalavyākule dhūlīpaṭale diviṣaddhvani dhikkṛtānyadhvanipaṭahadhvānabadhiritāśeṣadigantarālaṃ śastrāśastri hastāhasti parasparābhihatasainyaṃ janyamajani // Dkc_1,1.14 //
children.translated_text: Then, between the two [armies], in a cloud of dust that confused the expanse of the sky — as if it were a curtain-pavilion for the divine maidens who had come to choose husbands among the new warriors — [a cloud of dust] raised from the earth trampled by the hooves of chariot-horses, rooted in the streams of rut-fluid flowing from the temples of massed war-elephants — with the sound of drums deafening the entire space between the quarters, drowning out all other sounds — a battle arose, in which weapon clashed against weapon, hand against hand, elephant against elephant, army against army.

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.15:
tatra magadharājaḥ prakṣīṇasakalasainyamaṇḍalaṃ mālavarājaṃ jīvagrāhamabhigṛhya kṛpālutayā punarapi svarājye pratiṣṭhāpayāmāsa // Dkc_1,1.15 //
children.translated_text: There, the king of <s>Magadha</s>, having captured the king of <s>Mālava</s> alive when his entire army had been annihilated, out of compassion reinstated him in his own kingdom.

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.16:
tataḥ sa ratnākaramekhalāmilāmananyaśāsanāṃ śāsadanapatyatayā nārāyaṇaṃ sakalalokaikakāraṇaṃ nirantaramarcayāmāsa // Dkc_1,1.16 //
children.translated_text: Then, ruling the earth garlanded by the ocean, with no rival to his authority, he continuously worshipped <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), the sole cause of all worlds, because he was without a son.

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.17:
atha kadācittadagramahiṣī "devi! devena kalpavallīphalamāpnuhi' iti prabhātasamaye susvapnamavalokitavatī // Dkc_1,1.17 //
children.translated_text: Then once, his chief queen beheld an auspicious dream at dawn — 'O Queen! Obtain from the Lord the fruit of the wish-fulfilling creeper.'

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.18:
sā tadā dayitamanorathapuṣpabhūtaṃ garbhamadhatta // Dkc_1,1.18 //
children.translated_text: She then conceived a child, which was like the flower-bud of her beloved's desire.

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.19:
rājāpi sampannyakkṛtākhaṇḍalaḥ suhṛnnṛpamaṇḍalaṃ samāhūya nijasampanyanorathānurūpaṃ devyāḥ sīmantotsavaṃ vyadhatta // Dkc_1,1.19 //
children.translated_text: The king too, his splendor having surpassed that of <s>Indra</s>, summoning the circle of allied kings, performed the <s>sīmantotsava</s> (hair-parting ceremony) for the queen, befitting his own magnificent desires.

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.20:

ekadā hitaiḥ suhṛnmantripurohitaiḥ sabhāyāṃ siṃhāsanāsīno guṇairahīno lalāṭataṭanyastāñjalinā dvārapālena vyajñāpi-"deva! devasandarśanalālasamānasaḥ ko 'pi devena viracyārcanārhe yatirdvāradeśamadhyāste'iti // Dkc_1,1.20 //
children.translated_text: One day, while the king — in no way deficient in virtues — was seated on the throne in the assembly hall with his well-wishing ministers, counselors, and priests, the doorkeeper, with palms joined at his forehead, announced: 'Your Majesty! Some ascetic, whose mind eagerly seeks an audience with Your Majesty, fashioned by Your Majesty as one worthy of worship, waits at the entrance.'

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.21:
tadanujñātena tena saṃyamī nṛpasamīpamanāyi // Dkc_1,1.21 //
children.translated_text: Permitted by him, the ascetic was brought into the king's presence.

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.22:

bhūpatirāyāntaṃ taṃ vilokya samyagjñātatadīyagūḍhacārabhāvo nikhilamanucaranikaraṃ visṛjya mantrijanasametaḥ praṇatamenaṃ mandahāsamabhāṣata-"nanu tāpasa! deśaṃ sāpadeśaṃ bhramanbhavāṃstatra tatra bhavadabhijñātaṃ kathayatu'iti // Dkc_1,1.22 //
children.translated_text: The king, seeing him approach, having through his well-informed secret intelligence already understood his hidden movements, dismissed his entire retinue, and accompanied only by his counselors, addressed this bowing man with a gentle smile: 'O ascetic! Wandering through the land with a purpose, tell us what you have learned in various places through your knowledge.'

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.23:

tenābhāṣi bhūbhramaṇabalinā prāñjalinā-"deva! śirasi devasyājñāmādāyainaṃ nirdeṣaṃ veṣaṃ svīkṛtya mālavendranagaraṃ praviśya tatra gūḍhataraṃ vartamānastasya rājñaḥ samastamudantajātaṃ viditvā pratyāgamam // Dkc_1,1.23 //
children.translated_text: He spoke, with palms joined, empowered by his wandering across the earth: 'Your Majesty! Carrying Your Majesty's command upon my head, assuming this guileless disguise, I entered the capital of the lord of <s>Mālava</s>; dwelling there in deep concealment, having learned the entire account of that king, I have returned.

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.24:

mānī mānasāraḥ svasainikāyuṣmattāntarāye saṃparāye bhavataḥ parājayamanubhūya vailakṣyalakṣyahṛdayo vītadayo mahākālanivāsinaṃ kālīvilāsinamanaśvaraṃ maheśvaraṃ samārādhya tapaḥ prabhāvasantuṣṭādasmādekavīrārātighnīṃ bhayadāṃ gadāṃ labdhvātmānamapratibhaṭaṃ manyamāno mahābhibhāno bhavantamabhiyoktumudyuṅkte /
children.translated_text: <s>Mānasāra</s>, the proud one, his heart marked with the shame of having experienced defeat at Your Majesty's hands in the battle in which your soldiers [prevailed], bereft of mercy, having propitiated <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord <s>Śiva</s>) — the imperishable one, the player of <s>Kālī</s>, dwelling in [the temple of] <s>Mahākāla</s> — through austerity, having obtained from him, pleased by his austerity's power, a mace (<s>gadā</s>) called <s>Ekavīrārighnī</s> (Slayer of the Foes of the One Hero), which inspires fear — considering himself invincible, greatly deluded, he prepares to march against Your Majesty.

children.text: tataḥ paraṃ deva eva pramāṇam' iti // Dkc_1,1.24 //
children.translated_text: Beyond this, only Your Majesty is the authority [on what to do].'

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.25:
tadālocya niścitatatkṛtyairamātyai rājā vijñāpito 'bhūt-deva, nirupāyena devasahāyena yoddhumarātirāyāti /
children.translated_text: Having considered this, the ministers — who had determined [the course of] that affair — informed the king: 'Your Majesty, the enemy approaches to fight Your Majesty with an invincible ally [i.e., the divine weapon].

children.text: tasmādasmākaṃ yuddhaṃ sāṃpratamasāmpratam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, for us, battle at this time is inopportune.

children.text: sahasā durgasaṃśrayaḥ kāryaḥ'iti // Dkc_1,1.25 //
children.translated_text: A hasty retreat to a fortress should be undertaken.'

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.26:
tairbahudhā vijñāpito 'pyakharveṇa garveṇa virājamāno rājā tadvākyamakṛtyamityanādṛtya pratiyoddhumanā babhūva // Dkc_1,1.26 //
children.translated_text: Though entreated in many ways by them, the king, resplendent with undiminished pride, disregarded their words as improper and resolved to fight back. (Dkc 1,1.26)

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.27:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,1.27]

children.text: śitikaṇṭhadattaśaktisāro mānasāro yoddhumanasāmagrībhūya sāmagrīsameto 'kleśaṃ magadhadeśaṃ praviveśa // Dkc_1,1.27 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mānasāra</s>, whose power was granted by <s>Śitikaṇṭha</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), having assembled his forces ready for battle, entered the land of <s>Magadha</s> without difficulty. (Dkc 1,1.27)

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.28:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,1.28]

children.text: tadā tadākarṇya mantriṇo bhūmahendraṃ magadhendraṃ kathañcidanunīyaripubhirasādhye vindhyāṭavīmadhye 'varodhānmūlabalarakṣitānniveśayāmāsuḥ // Dkc_1,1.28 //
children.translated_text: Then, upon hearing that, the ministers somehow pacified <s>Bhūmahendra</s>, the lord of <s>Magadha</s>, and settled him along with his harem and main army in a protected position in the midst of the <s>Vindhya</s> forest, which was impregnable to enemies. (Dkc 1,1.28)

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.29:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,1.29]

children.text: rājahaṃsastu praśastavītadainyasainyasametastīvragatyā nirgatyādhikaruṣaṃ dviṣaṃ rurodha // Dkc_1,1.29 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rājahaṃsa</s>, accompanied by his army of praised valor and free from despondency, sallied forth swiftly and besieged the exceedingly wrathful enemy. (Dkc 1,1.29)

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.30:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,1.30]

children.text: parasparabaddhavairayoretayoḥ śūrayostadā tadālokanakutūhalāgatagaganacarāścaryakāraṇe raṇe vartamāne jayākāṅkṣī mālavadeśarakṣī vividhāyudhasthairyacaryāñcitasamaratulitāmareśvarasya magadheśvarasya tasyopari purā purārātidattāṃ gadāṃ prāhiṇot // Dkc_1,1.30 //
children.translated_text: As those two heroes, bound in mutual enmity, were engaged in a battle so wondrous that celestial beings came in the sky out of curiosity to witness it, the protector of the <s>Mālava</s> land, desiring victory, hurled at the lord of <s>Magadha</s> — who in the contest of battle matched <s>Indra</s> himself in steadfastness with various weapons — the mace formerly bestowed by <s>Purārāti</s> (<s>Śiva</s>, the enemy of the cities). (Dkc 1,1.30)

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.31:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,1.31]

children.text: niśitaśaranikaraśakalīkṛtāpi sā paśupatiśāsanasyāvandhyatayā sūtaṃ nihatya rathasthaṃ rājānaṃ mūrchitamakārṣīt // Dkc_1,1.31 //
children.translated_text: Though shattered into fragments by a shower of sharp arrows, that [mace], by the unfailing nature of <s>Paśupati's</s> (<s>Śiva's</s>) decree, slew the charioteer and rendered the king, who was standing in his chariot, unconscious. (Dkc 1,1.31)

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.32:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,1.32]

children.text: tato vītapragrahā akṣatavigrahā vāhā rathamādāya daivagatyāntaḥpuraśaraṇyaṃ mahāraṇyaṃ prāviśan // Dkc_1,1.32 //
children.translated_text: Then the horses, freed from their reins and with bodies uninjured, carried the chariot away, and by the course of fate entered the great forest, which was a refuge [as secure as] the inner palace. (Dkc 1,1.32)

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.33:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,1.33]

children.text: mālavanātho jayalakṣmīsanātho magadharājyaṃ prājyaṃ samākramya puṣpapuramadhyatiṣṭhat // Dkc_1,1.33 //
children.translated_text: The lord of <s>Mālava</s>, ever possessed of the goddess of victory, overran the prosperous kingdom of <s>Magadha</s> and took up residence in <s>Puṣpapura</s> (<s>Pāṭaliputra</s>). (Dkc 1,1.33)

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.34:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,1.34]

children.text: tatra hetitatihatiśrāntā amātyā daivagatyānutkrāntajīvitā niśāntavātalabdhasaṃjñāḥ kathañcidāśvasya rājānaṃ samantādanvīkṣyānavalokitavanto dainyavanto devīmavāpuḥ // Dkc_1,1.34 //
children.translated_text: There, the ministers, exhausted from the blows of weapons, their lives spared only by the course of fate, having regained consciousness through the night-end breeze, somehow revived and, looking all around for the king but not finding him, were filled with despondency and [eventually] reached the queen. (Dkc 1,1.34)

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.35:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,1.35]

children.text: vasumatī tu tebhyo nikhilasainyakṣatiṃ rājño 'dṛśyatvaṃ cākarṇyodvignā śokasāgaramagnā ramaṇānugamane matiṃ vyadhatta // Dkc_1,1.35 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vasumatī</s>, upon hearing from them of the complete destruction of the army and the disappearance of the king, was distressed and, submerged in an ocean of grief, set her mind upon following her husband [in death]. (Dkc 1,1.35)

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.36:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,1.36]

children.text: `kalyāṇi, bhūramaṇamaraṇamaniścitam /
children.translated_text: 'O auspicious lady, the death of the lord of the earth is uncertain;

children.text: kiñca daivajñakathito mathitoddhatārātiḥ sārvabhaumo 'bhirāmo bhavitā sukumāraḥ kumārastvadudare vasati /
children.translated_text: moreover, the astrologers have foretold that a prince who will be a universal sovereign, delightful and crusher of arrogant enemies, dwells in your womb;

children.text: tasmādadya tava maraṇamanucitam' iti bhūṣitabhāṣitairamātyapurohitairanunīyamānayā tayā kṣaṇaṃ kṣaṇahīnayā tūṣṇīmasthāyi // Dkc_1,1.36 //
children.translated_text: therefore your death today is unfitting' — thus dissuaded by the ministers and the family priest with well-adorned words, she, whose every moment was [as if] bereft of a moment [of life], remained silent. (Dkc 1,1.36)

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.37:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,1.37]

children.text: athārdharātre nidrānilīnanetre parijane vijane śokapārāvāramapāramuttartumaśaknuvatī senāniveśadeśaṃ niḥśabdaleśaṃ śanairatikramya yasmin rathasya saṃsaktatayā tadānayanapalāyanaśrāntā gantumakṣamāḥ kṣamāpatirathyāḥ pathyākulāḥ pūrvamatiṣṭhaṃstasya nikaṭavaṭataroḥ śākhāyāṃ mṛtirekhāyāmiva kvaciduttarīyārddhena bandhanaṃ mṛtisādhanaṃ viracya martukāmābhirāmā vāṅmādhurīvirasīkṛtakala-kaṇṭha-kaṇṭhā sāśrukaṇṭhā vyalapat-"lāvaṇyopamitapuṣpasāyaka, bhūnāyaka, bhavāneva bhāvinyapi janmani vallabho bhavatu' iti // Dkc_1,1.37 //
children.translated_text: Then, at midnight, when the attendants had their eyes closed in sleep, in that deserted [place], unable to cross the shoreless ocean of grief, she silently passed beyond the precincts of the military encampment, and at a branch of a nearby banyan tree — where the horses of the royal road, exhausted from the effort of dragging the chariot and unable to go further, had previously stood entangled on the congested road — she fashioned a noose with half of her upper garment, as if upon the line of death, an instrument of dying. The beautiful lady, desiring death, whose throat surpassed the voice of the <s>kalakantha</s> (cuckoo) in sweetness of speech, yet now choked with tears, cried out: 'O lord of the earth, likened to the flower-arrowed [<s>Kāmadeva</s>] in charm, may you alone be my beloved in the next birth too!' (Dkc 1,1.37)

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.38:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,1.38]

children.text: tadākarṇya nīhārakarakiraṇanikarasaṃparkalabdhāvabodho māgadho 'gādharudhiravikṣaraṇanaṣṭaceṣṭo devīvākyameva niścinvānastanvānaḥ priyavacanāni śanaistāmāhvayat // Dkc_1,1.38 //
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the king of <s>Magadha</s>, who had regained consciousness through the contact of the cool moonbeam-like rays of mist, [but] whose movements had ceased due to the profuse flow of blood, pondering only the queen's words and uttering loving words, softly called out to her. (Dkc 1,1.38)

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.39:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,1.39]

children.text: sā sasaṃbhramamāgatyāmandahṛdayānandasaṃphullavadanāravindā tamupoṣitābhyāmivānimiṣitābhyāṃ locanābhyāṃ pibantī vikasvareṇa svareṇa purohitāmātyajanamuccairāhūya tebhyastamadarśayat // Dkc_1,1.39 //
children.translated_text: She, rushing to him in haste, her lotus-face blossoming with boundless joy of heart, drinking him in as it were with her unblinking eyes that seemed to have been fasting [from the sight of him], loudly summoned the family priest and the ministers, and showed him to them. (Dkc 1,1.39)

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.40:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,1.40]

children.text: rājā niṭilataṭacumbitanijacaraṇāmbujaiḥ praśaṃsitadaivamāhātmyairamātyairabhāṇi-"deva, rathyacayaḥ sārathyapagame rathaṃ rabhasādaraṇyamanayat'iti // Dkc_1,1.40 //
children.translated_text: The king was addressed by the ministers, who touched his lotus-feet to their foreheads and praised the greatness of fate: 'Lord, the team of horses, upon the departure of the charioteer, swiftly carried the chariot into the forest.' (Dkc 1,1.40)

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.41:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,1.41]

children.text: `tatra nihatasainikagrāme saṃgrāme mālavapatinārādhitapurārātinā prahitayā gadayā dayāhīnena tāḍito mūrchāmāgatyātra vane niśāntapavanena bodhito 'bhavam' iti mahīpatirakathayat // Dkc_1,1.41 //
children.translated_text: 'There, in the battle in which the soldiers were slain, struck by the mace sent by the lord of <s>Mālava</s>, who had propitiated <s>Purārāti</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), merciless [as he was], I fell into unconsciousness, and was awakened here in the forest by the night-end breeze' — thus the king narrated. (Dkc 1,1.41)

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.42:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,1.42]

children.text: tato viracitamahena mantrinivahena viracitadaivānukūlyena kālena śiviramānīyāpanītāśeṣaśalyo vikasita-nijānanāravindo rājā sahasā viropitavraṇo 'kāri // Dkc_1,1.42 //
children.translated_text: Then, through the efforts of the assembled ministers and through the favorable course of time, the king was brought to a camp, all his arrow-wounds were removed, and with his own lotus-face blooming [again], his wounds were quickly healed. (Dkc 1,1.42)

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.43:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,1.43]

children.text: virodhidaivadhikkṛtapuruṣakāro dainyavyāptākāro magadhādhipatiradhikādhiramātyasaṃmatyā mṛdubhāṣitayā tayā vasumatyā matyā kalitayā ca samabodhi // Dkc_1,1.43 //
children.translated_text: The lord of <s>Magadha</s>, whose human effort had been thwarted by adverse fate, his form pervaded by despondency, was consoled through the counsel of the chief minister, through the gentle speech of <s>Vasumatī</s>, and through deliberation. (Dkc 1,1.43)

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.44:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,1.44]

children.text: `deva, sakalasya bhūpālakulasya madhye tejovariṣṭho gariṣṭho bhavānadya vindhyavanamadhyaṃ nivasatīti jalabudbudasamānā virājamānā sampattaḍillateva sahasaivodeti naśyati ca /
children.translated_text: 'Lord, among the entire lineage of kings, you are the foremost and most distinguished in splendor, yet today you dwell in the midst of the <s>Vindhya</s> forest — [but] royal fortune, equal to a water bubble, like a flash of lightning, suddenly rises and suddenly perishes;

children.text: tannikhilaṃ daivāyattamevāvadhārya kāryam // Dkc_1,1.44 //
children.translated_text: therefore, understanding all this to be entirely dependent on fate, one should act accordingly. (Dkc 1,1.44)

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.45:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,1.45]

children.text: kiñca purā hariścandrarāmacandramukhyā asaṃkhyā mahīndrā aiśvaryopamitamahendrā daivatantraṃ duḥkhayantraṃ samyaganubhūya paścādanekakālaṃ nijarājyamakurvan /
children.translated_text: Moreover, in the past, innumerable great kings such as <s>Hariścandra</s> and <s>Rāmacandra</s>, mighty as <s>Indra</s> in their sovereignty, having fully experienced the machine of suffering [driven by] the mechanism of fate, afterward ruled their own kingdoms for a long time.

children.text: tadvadeva bhavānbhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: Just so shall you [rule again].

children.text: kañcana kālaṃ viracitadaivasamādhirvigalitādhistiṣṭhatu tāvat iti // Dkc_1,1.45 //
children.translated_text: For some time, having made peace with fate, let [the king] remain free from anxiety.' (Dkc 1,1.45)

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.46:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,1.46]

children.text: tataḥ sakalasainyasamanvito rājahaṃsastapovibhrājamānaṃ vāmadevanāmānaṃ tapodhanaṃ nijābhilāṣāvāptisādhanaṃ jagāma // Dkc_1,1.46 //
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rājahaṃsa</s>, accompanied by his entire army, went to an ascetic named <s>Vāmadeva</s>, resplendent with <s>tapas</s> (austerity), a rich treasury of asceticism, the means for attaining his own desire. (Dkc 1,1.46)

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.47:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,1.47]

children.text: taṃ praṇamya tena kṛtātithyastasmai kathitakathyastadāśrame dūrīkṛtaśrame kañcana kālamuṣitvā nijarājyābhilāṣī mitabhāṣī somakulāvataṃso rājahaṃso munimabhāṣata-"bhagavan, mānasāraḥ prabalena daivabalena māṃ nirjitya madbhogyaṃ rājyamanubhavati /
children.translated_text: Having bowed to him and been received hospitably by him, having told him all that was to be told, <s>Rājahaṃsa</s>, the ornament of the <s>Soma</s> dynasty, having stayed for some time in that hermitage free from toil, desirous of [regaining] his own kingdom and sparing of speech, said to the sage: 'Venerable sir, <s>Mānasāra</s>, by the mighty power of fate, having defeated me, enjoys the kingdom that should be mine;

children.text: tadvadahamapyugraṃ tapo viracya tamarātimunmūlayiṣyāmi lokaśaraṇyena bhavatkāruṇyeneti niyamavantaṃ bhavantaṃ prāpnavam' iti // Dkc_1,1.47 //
children.translated_text: therefore I too, performing fierce <s>tapas</s> (austerity), shall uproot that enemy — [and it is] with [hope in] your compassion, which is a refuge for the world, that I have come to you who are bound by [ascetic] vows.' (Dkc 1,1.47)

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.48:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,1.48]

children.text: tatastrikālajñastapodhano rājānamavocat-sakhe! śarīrakārśyakāriṇā tapasālam /
children.translated_text: Then the ascetic, who knew the three times [past, present, and future], said to the king: 'Friend! Enough of this austerity that causes emaciation of the body.

children.text: vasumatīgarbhasthaḥ sakalaripukulamardano rājanandano nūnaṃ sambhaviṣyati, kañcana kālaṃ tūṣṇīmāssva'iti // Dkc_1,1.48 //
children.translated_text: A royal son who will crush the entire lineage of enemies shall certainly be born from the womb of <s>Vasumatī</s>; for some time, remain silent [and wait].' (Dkc 1,1.48)

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.49:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,1.49]

children.text: gaganacāriṇyāpi vāṇyā "satyametat' iti tadevāvāci /
children.translated_text: A celestial voice too proclaimed: 'This is true.'

children.text: rājāpi munivākya maṅgīkṛtyātiṣṭhat // Dkc_1,1.49 //
children.translated_text: The king also accepted the sage's words and remained [patient]. (Dkc 1,1.49)

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.50:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,1.50]

children.text: tataḥ sampūrṇagarbhadivasā vasumatī sumuhūrte sakalalakṣaṇalakṣitaṃ sutamasūta /
children.translated_text: Then, when the days of her pregnancy were complete, <s>Vasumatī</s> gave birth at an auspicious moment to a son endowed with all [auspicious] marks.

children.text: brahmavarcasena tulitavedhasaṃ purodhasaṃ puraskṛtya kṛtyavinmahīpatiḥ kumāraṃ sukumāraṃ jātasaṃskāreṇa bālālaṅkāreṇa ca virājamānaṃ rājavāhananāmānaṃ vyadhatta // Dkc_1,1.50 //
children.translated_text: The king, knower of duty, placing at the fore the family priest whose splendor equaled that of <s>Brahmā</s>, performed the birth-rites (<s>jātasaṃskāra</s>) and the infant-adornment ceremonies, and bestowed upon the radiant, delicate prince the name <s>Rājavāhana</s>. (Dkc 1,1.50)

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.51:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,1.51]

children.text: tasminneva kāle sumatisumitrasumantrasuśrutānāṃ mantriṇāṃ pramatimitraguptayantraguptaviśrutākhyā mahābhikhyāḥ sūnavo navodyadindurucaścirāyuṣaḥ samajāyanta /
children.translated_text: At that very time, to the ministers <s>Sumati</s>, <s>Sumitra</s>, <s>Sumantra</s>, and <s>Suśruta</s>, were born sons named <s>Pramati</s>, <s>Mitragupta</s>, <s>Yantragupta</s>, and <s>Viśruta</s> — of great renown, radiant as the newly risen moon, and long-lived.

children.text: rājavāhano mantriputrairātmamitraiḥ saha bālakelīranubhavannavardhata // Dkc_1,1.51 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rājavāhana</s> grew up enjoying childhood games together with the ministers' sons, who were his own friends. (Dkc 1,1.51)

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.52:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,1.52]

children.text: atha kadācidekena tāpasena rasena rājalakṣaṇavirājitaṃ kaccinnayanānandakaraṃ sukumāraṃ kumāraṃ rājñe samarpyāvoci-bhūvallabha, kuśasamidānayanāya vanaṃ gatena mayā kācidaśaraṇyā vyaktakārpaṇyāśru muñcantī vanitā vilokitā // Dkc_1,1.52 //
children.translated_text: Then one day, a certain ascetic presented to the king a delicate prince, adorned with the marks of royalty and delightful to the eyes, and said: 'O lord of the earth, while I had gone to the forest to fetch <s>kuśa</s> grass and firewood, I beheld a woman, shelterless, shedding tears of manifest wretchedness.' (Dkc 1,1.52)

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.53:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,1.53]

children.text: nirjane vane kiṃnimittaṃ rudyate tvayā iti pṛṣṭā sā karasaroruhairaśru pramṛjya sagadgadaṃ māmavocat-mune, lāvaṇyajitapuṣpasāyake mithilānāyake kīrtivyāptasudharmaṇi nijasuhṛdo magadharājasya sīmantinīsīmantamahotsavāya putradārasamanvite puṣpapuramupetya kañcana kālamadhivasati samārādhitagirīśo mālavādhīśo magadharājaṃ yoddhumabhyagāt // Dkc_1,1.53 //
children.translated_text: When asked 'Why do you weep in this deserted forest?', she, wiping her tears with her lotus-like hands, spoke to me with a choked voice: 'O sage, when the king of <s>Mithilā</s>, whose beauty defeats the flower-arrowed [god of love], whose virtue had spread his fame — when he had come to <s>Puṣpapura</s> with wife and son for the joyous [ceremony] at the hair-parting of the queen of his friend the king of <s>Magadha</s>, and was dwelling there for some time — the lord of <s>Mālava</s>, having propitiated Lord <s>Śiva</s>, marched forth to wage war against the king of <s>Magadha</s>.' [Dkc 1.1.53]

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.54:
children.translated_text: [section marker]

children.text: tatra prakhyātayoretayorasaṅkhye saṅkhye vartamāne suhṛtsāhāyyakaṃ kurvāṇo nijabale sati videhe videheśvaraḥ prahāravarmā jayavatā ripuṇābhigṛhya kāruṇyena puṇyena visṛṣṭo hatāvaśeṣeṇa śūnyena sainyena saha svapuragamanamakarot // Dkc_1,1.54 //
children.translated_text: 'In the fierce, innumerable battle between those two famous [kings], <s>Prahāravarman</s>, the lord of <s>Videha</s>, having his own army and rendering aid to his friend, was captured by the victorious enemy but released out of compassion — and with his army mostly destroyed, with the remnant of his forces, he set out for his own city.' [Dkc 1.1.54]

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.55:
children.translated_text: [section marker]

children.text: tato vanamārgeṇa durgeṇa gacchannadhikabalena śabarabalena rabhasādabhihanyamāno mūlabalābhirakṣitāvarodhaḥ sa mahānirodhaḥ palāyiṣṭa /
tadīyārbhakayoryamayordhātrībhāvena parikalpitāhaṃ madduhitāpi tīvragatiṃ bhūpatimanugantumakṣame abhūva /
children.translated_text: 'I, who had been appointed as nurse to his twin sons, along with my own daughter, was unable to follow the king who moved with great speed.'

children.text: tatra vivṛtavadanaḥ ko 'pi rūpīkopa iva vyāghraḥ śīghraṃ māmāghrātumāgatavān /
children.translated_text: 'There, some tiger — like fury incarnate with gaping jaws — came swiftly to devour me.'

children.text: bhītāhamudagragrāvṇi skhalantī paryapatam /
children.translated_text: 'Frightened, I stumbled on the high boulders and fell.'

children.text: madīyapāṇibhraṣṭo bālakaḥ kasyāpi kapilāśavasya kroḍamabhyalīyata // Dkc_1,1.55 //
children.translated_text: 'The baby boy, slipping from my hands, clung to the breast of some tawny mare.' [Dkc 1.1.55]

'Then, as he traveled through a difficult forest path, being vehemently attacked by a superior <s>Śabara</s> (tribal) force, he — his harem protected by the core troops — that great [king in] great distress fled.'

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.56:
children.translated_text: [section marker]

children.text: tacchavākarṣiṇo 'marṣiṇo vyāghrasya prāṇānbāṇo bāṇāsanayantramukto 'pāharat /
lolālako bālako 'pi śabarairādāya kutracidupānīyata /
children.translated_text: 'The curly-haired baby too was carried off somewhere by the <s>Śabaras</s>.'

children.text: kumāramaparamudvahantī madduhitā kutra gatā na jāne /
children.translated_text: 'Where my daughter, carrying the other prince, went — I do not know.'

children.text: sāhaṃ mohaṃ gatā kenāpi kṛpālunā vṛṣṇipālena svakuṭīramāveśya viropitavraṇābhavam /
children.translated_text: 'I, having fainted, was brought into his hut by some compassionate <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> tribesman, and my wounds were healed.'

children.text: tataḥ svasthībhūya kṣmābharturantikamupatiṣṭhāsurasahāyatayā duhituranabhijñatayā ca vyākulībhavāmi-ityabhidadhānā "ekākinyapi svāminaṃ gamiṣyāmi' iti sā tadaiva niragāt // Dkc_1,1.56 //
children.translated_text: 'Then, having recovered, I became distressed — unable to attend upon the king, being alone, and not knowing where my daughter was.' Having said this, [she declared] 'Even alone, I shall go to my lord,' and she departed at once. [Dkc 1.1.56]
'An arrow released from a bow-machine took the life of the furious tiger that was dragging that corpse [of the mare].'

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.57:
children.translated_text: [section marker]

children.text: ahamapi bhavanmitrasya videhanāthasya vipannimittaṃ viṣādamanubhavaṃstadanvayāṅkuraṃ kumāramanviṣyaṃstadaikaṃ caṇḍikāmandiraṃ sundaraṃ prāgām // Dkc_1,1.57 //
children.translated_text: 'I too, experiencing sorrow at the misfortune of the lord of <s>Videha</s>, your friend, went searching for the prince — the sprout of his lineage — and came to a certain beautiful temple of <s>Caṇḍikā</s>.' [Dkc 1.1.57]

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.58:
children.translated_text: [section marker]

children.text: tatra saṃtatamevaṃvidhavijayasiddhaye kumāraṃ devatopahāraṃ kariṣyantaḥ kirātāḥ "mahāruhaśākhāvalambitamenamasilatayā vā, saikatatale khanananikṣiptacaraṇaṃ lakṣīkṛtya śitaśaranikareṇa vā, anekacaraṇaiḥ palāyamānaṃ kukkurabālakairvā daṃśayitvā saṃhaniṣyāmaḥ' iti bhāṣamāṇā mayā samabhyabhāṣanta "nanu kirātottamāḥ, ghorapracāre kāntāre skhalitapathaḥ sthavirabhūsuro 'haṃ mama putrakaṃ kvacicchāyāyāṃ nikṣipya mārgānveṣaṇāya kiñcidantaramagaccham // Dkc_1,1.58 //
children.translated_text: 'There, <s>Kirātas</s> (tribal hunters), intending to offer the boy as an oblation to the goddess for the success of just such a continuous victory, were saying: "We shall kill him by hanging him from the branch of a great tree by a cord, or by burying him up to his feet in sand and striking him with a shower of sharp arrows, or by having young hunting dogs bite him as he runs away on his many legs [i.e., crawling]." I addressed them: "Hear, O best of <s>Kirātas</s>! I am an aged <s>Brahmin</s> who has lost his way in this forest of terrible paths. I left my little son somewhere in the shade and went a short distance to search for the road.' [Dkc 1.1.58]

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.59:
children.translated_text: [section marker]

children.text: sa kutra gataḥ, kena vā gṛhītaḥ, parīkṣyāpi na vīkṣyate tanmukhāvalokanena vinānekānyahānyatītāni /
children.translated_text: 'Where has he gone, or by whom has he been taken? Even after searching, he cannot be seen; many days have passed without seeing his face.'

children.text: kiṃ karomi, kva yāmi bhavadbhirna kimadarśi iti // Dkc_1,1.59 //
children.translated_text: 'What should I do? Where should I go? Have you not seen [anything]?' [Dkc 1.1.59]

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.60:
children.translated_text: [section marker]

children.text: `dvijottama! kaścidatra tiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: '"O excellent <s>Brahmin</s>! A certain [child] is here.'

children.text: kimeṣa tava nandanaḥ satyameva /
children.translated_text: 'Is this your son? Indeed it is!'

children.text: tadenaṃ gṛhāṇa' ityuktvā daivānukūlyena mahyaṃ taṃ vyataran // Dkc_1,1.60 //
children.translated_text: 'Then take him" — saying this, by divine favor, they handed him over to me.' [Dkc 1.1.60]

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.61:
children.translated_text: [section marker]

children.text: tebhyo dattāśīrahaṃ bālakamaṅgīkṛtya śiśirodakādinopacāreṇāśvāsya niḥśaṅkaṃ bhavadaṅkaṃ samānītavānasmi /
children.translated_text: 'Having blessed them, I took the baby boy, revived him with cool water and other ministrations, and brought him fearlessly to your lap.'

children.text: enamāyuṣmantaṃ pitṛrūpo bhavānabhirakṣatāt'iti // Dkc_1,1.61 //
children.translated_text: 'May Your Lordship, who is like a father to him, protect this long-lived [child].' [Dkc 1.1.61]

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.62:
children.translated_text: [section marker]

children.text: rājā suhṛdāpannimittaṃ śokaṃ tannandanavilokanasukhena kiñcidadharīkṛtya tamupahāravarmanāmnāhūya rājavāhanamiva pupoṣa // Dkc_1,1.62 //
children.translated_text: 'The king, having somewhat subdued his grief over his friend's misfortune by the joy of seeing his [friend's] son, called him <s>Upahāravarman</s> and raised him like a royal steed.' [Dkc 1.1.62]

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.63:
children.translated_text: [section marker]

children.text: janapatirekasmin puṇyadivase tīrthasnānāya pakvaṇanikaṭamārgeṇa gacchannabalayā kayācidupalālitamanupamaśarīraṃ kumāraṃ kañcidavalokya kutūhalākulastāmapṛcchat-"bhāmini! ruciramūrtiḥ sarājaguṇasaṃpūrtirasāvarbhako bhavadanvayasaṃbhavo na bhavati kasya nayanānandaḥ, nimittena kena bhavadadhīno jātaḥ kathyatāṃ yāthātathyena tvayā' iti // Dkc_1,1.63 //
children.translated_text: 'One auspicious day, the king, going by a road near the marketplace for a holy bath at a pilgrimage site, saw a certain boy of incomparable form being fondled by some low-born woman. Curious, he asked her: "Fair lady! This beautiful boy, complete with all royal qualities — he does not appear to be born of your family. Whose delight of the eyes is he? By what circumstance did he come into your care? Tell me the truth."' [Dkc 1.1.63]

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.64:
children.translated_text: [section marker]

children.text: praṇatayā tayā śabaryā salīlamalāpi-"rājan! ātmapallīsamīpe padavyāṃ vartamānasya śakrasamānasya mithileśvarasya sarvasvamapaharati śabarasainye maddayitenāpahṛtya kumāra eṣa mahyamarpito vyavardhata iti // Dkc_1,1.64 //
children.translated_text: 'Bowing, that <s>Śabara</s> woman said, somewhat bashfully: "O king! When the <s>Śabara</s> army was plundering the entire wealth of the lord of <s>Mithilā</s>, who was equal to <s>Śakra</s> [i.e., <s>Indra</s>], on a road near our village — this prince was carried off by my husband and given to me, and he has grown up [thus]."' [Dkc 1.1.64]

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.65:
children.translated_text: [section marker]

children.text: tadavadhārya kāryajño rājā munikathitaṃ dvitīyaṃ rājakumārameva niścitya sāmadānābhyāṃ tāmanunīyāpahāravarmetyākhyāya devyai "vardhaya' iti samarpitavān // Dkc_1,1.65 //
children.translated_text: 'Having ascertained this, the king, knowing what was to be done, determined this to be the second royal prince as described by the sage. Persuading her with conciliation and gifts, and naming him <s>Apahāravarman</s>, he entrusted him to the queen [saying] "Raise him."' [Dkc 1.1.65]

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.66:
children.translated_text: [section marker]

children.text: kadācidvāmadevaśiṣyaḥ somadevaśarmā nāma kañcidekaṃ bālakaṃ rājñaḥ puro nikṣipyābhāṣata-deva! rāmatīrthe snātvā pratyāgacchatā mayā kānanāvanau vanitayā kayāpi dhāryamāṇamenamujjvalākāraṃ kumāraṃ vilokya sādaramabhāṇi--"sthavire! kā tvam? etasminnaṭavīmadhye bālakamudvahantī kimarthamāyāsena bhramasi' iti // Dkc_1,1.66 //
children.translated_text: 'Once, a disciple of <s>Vāmadeva</s> named <s>Somadevaśarman</s> placed a certain baby boy before the king and said: "Lord! As I was returning from bathing at <s>Rāmatīrtha</s>, I saw this radiant boy being carried by some woman in the forest wilderness, and I respectfully addressed her: 'Elder woman! Who are you? Why do you wander with effort in the midst of this forest, carrying a baby boy?'"' [Dkc 1.1.66]

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.67:
children.translated_text: [section marker]

children.text: vṛddhayāpyabhāṣi-"munivara! kālayavananāmni dvīpe kālagupto nāma dhanāḍhyo vaiśyavaraḥ kaścidasti /
children.translated_text: 'The old woman replied: "O best of sages! On an island called <s>Kālayavana</s>, there lives a certain wealthy merchant of the <s>Vaiśya</s> caste named <s>Kālagupta</s>.'

children.text: tannandinīṃ nayanānandakāriṇīṃ suvṛttāṃ nāmaitasmād dvīpādāgato magadhanāthamantrisaṃbhavo ratnodbhavo nāma ramaṇīyaguṇālayo bhrāntabhūvalayo manohārī vyavahāryupayamya suvastusaṃpadā śvaśureṇa saṃmānito 'bhūt /
children.translated_text: 'A man named <s>Ratnodbhava</s>, born of the minister of the lord of <s>Magadha</s>, who had come from this continent — charming, an abode of delightful qualities, who had wandered the earth — married his daughter named <s>Suvṛttā</s>, a delight to the eyes, and was honored by his father-in-law with an abundance of fine wealth.'

children.text: kālakrameṇa natāṅgī garbhiṇī jātā // Dkc_1,1.67 //
children.translated_text: 'In time, the slender-limbed [<s>Suvṛttā</s>] became pregnant.' [Dkc 1.1.67]

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.68:
children.translated_text: [section marker]

children.text: tataḥ sodaravilokanakautūhalena ratnodbhavaḥ kathañcicchvaśuramanunīya capalalocanayā saha pravahaṇamāruhya puṣpapuramabhipratasthe /
children.translated_text: 'Then, <s>Ratnodbhava</s>, eager to see his kinsmen, somehow persuaded his father-in-law, and boarding a ship with his restless-eyed [wife], set out for <s>Puṣpapura</s>.'

children.text: kallolamālikābhihataḥ potaḥ samudrāmbhasyamajjat // Dkc_1,1.68 //
children.translated_text: 'The boat, struck by garlands of waves, sank in the ocean waters.' [Dkc 1.1.68]

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.69:
children.translated_text: [section marker]

children.text: garbhabharālasāṃ tāṃ lalanāṃ dhātrībhāvena kalpitāhaṃ karābhyāmudvahantī phalakamekamadhiruhya daivagatyā tīrabhūmimagamam /
suhṛjjanaparivṛto ratnodbhavastatra nimagno vā kenopāyena tīramagamadvā na jānāmi /
children.translated_text: 'Whether <s>Ratnodbhava</s>, surrounded by his people, drowned there, or by what means he reached the shore — I do not know.'

children.text: kleśasya parāṃ kāṣṭhāmadhigatā suvṛttāsminnaṭavīmadhye 'dya sutamasūta /
children.translated_text: '<s>Suvṛttā</s>, having reached the utmost limit of distress, gave birth today to a son in the midst of this forest.'

children.text: prasavavedanayā vicetanā sā pracchāyaśītale tarutale nivasati /
children.translated_text: 'Unconscious from the pain of childbirth, she lies at the foot of a shady, cool tree.'

children.text: vijane vane sthātumaśakyatayā janapadagāminaṃ mārgamanveṣṭumudyuktayā mayā vivaśāyāstasyāḥ samīpe bālakaṃ nikṣipya gantumanucitamiti kumāro 'pyanāyi iti // Dkc_1,1.69 //
children.translated_text: 'Since it is impossible to stay in this deserted forest, I set out to search for a road leading to habitation; but it would be improper for me, helpless as I am, to leave the baby near her and go — so the boy too was brought along.'"' [Dkc 1.1.69]
'Carrying that young woman, sluggish from the weight of her pregnancy, in my arms — for I had been appointed as her nurse — I mounted a plank and by the decree of fate reached the shore.'

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.70:
children.translated_text: [section marker]

children.text:
tasminneva kṣaṇe vanyo vāraṇaḥ kaścidadṛśyata /
taṃ vilokya bhītā sā bālakaṃ nipātya prādravat /
ahaṃ samīpalatāgulmake praviśya parīkṣamāṇo 'tiṣṭham, nipatitaṃ bālakaṃ pallavakavalamivādadati gajapatau kaṇṭhīravo mahāgraheṇa nyapatat /
children.translated_text: 'While I hid in a nearby thicket of creepers and observed, as the lord of elephants was picking up the fallen baby like a mouthful of leaves, a lion pounced upon [the elephant] with a mighty leap.'

children.text: bhayākulena dantāvalena jhaṭiti viyati samutpātyamāno bālako nyapatat /
children.translated_text: 'The baby, being tossed into the air by the panic-stricken elephant, fell down.'

children.text: cirāyuṣmattayā sa connatataruśākhāsamāsīnena vānareṇa kenacitpakvaphalabuddhyā parigṛhya phaletaratayā vitataskandhamūle nikṣipto 'bhūt /
children.translated_text: 'By virtue of his long lifespan, some monkey sitting on the branch of a tall tree grasped him thinking he was a ripe fruit, and finding him to be something other than a fruit, placed him at the base of an outstretched tree trunk.'

children.text: so 'pi markaṭaḥ kvacidagāt // Dkc_1,1.70 //
children.translated_text: 'That monkey too went off somewhere.' [Dkc 1.1.70]
'At that very moment, a wild elephant appeared. Seeing it, she dropped the baby in fright and ran away.'

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.71:
children.translated_text: [section marker]

children.text: bālakena sattvasaṃpannatayā sakalakleśasahenābhāvi /
children.translated_text: 'The baby, being endowed with inner strength, endured all this suffering.'

children.text: kesariṇā kariṇaṃ nihatya kutracidagāmi /
children.translated_text: 'The lion, having killed the elephant, went off somewhere.'

children.text: latāgṛhānnirgato 'hamapi tejaḥpuñjaṃ bālakaṃ śanairavanīruhādavatārya vanāntare vani tāmanviṣyāvilokyainamānīya gurave nivedya tannideśena bhavannikaṭamānītavānasmi'iti // Dkc_1,1.71 //
children.translated_text: 'I too, coming out from the bower of creepers, slowly brought the boy — that mass of radiance — down from the tree, searched for the woman in the forest, and not finding her, brought [the boy], reported to my teacher, and by his direction brought him into your presence.' [Dkc 1.1.71]

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.72:
children.translated_text: [section marker]

children.text: sarveṣāṃ suhṛdāmekadaivānukūladaivābhāvena mahadāścaryaṃ vibhrāṇo rājā "ratnodbhavaḥ kathamabhavat' iti cintayaṃstannandanaṃ puṣpodbhavanāmadheyaṃ vidhāya tadudantaṃ vyākhyāya suśrutāya viṣādasaṃtoṣāvanubhavaṃstadanujatanayaṃ samarpitavān // Dkc_1,1.72 //
children.translated_text: The king, greatly astonished at the absence of favorable destiny for all his friends at once, wondering 'How did <s>Ratnodbhava</s> come to be?', named his son <s>Puṣpodbhava</s>, narrated that story, and experiencing both grief and consolation toward <s>Suśruta</s>, entrusted to him the son of his younger brother. // Dkc_1,1.72 //

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.73:
children.translated_text: START Dkc 1,1.73:

children.text: anyedyuḥ kañcana bālakamurasi dadhatī vasumatīvallabhamabhigatā /
children.translated_text: On another day, a certain woman holding a baby boy on her breast approached the lord of the earth /

children.text: tena "kutratyo 'yam iti pṛṣṭā samabhāṣata-"rājan! atītāyāṃ rātrau kācana divyavanitā matpurataḥ kumāramenaṃ saṃsthāpya nidrāmudritāṃ māṃ vibodhya vinītābravīt-"devi! tvanmantriṇo dharmapālanandanasya kāmapālasya vallabhā yakṣakanyāhaṃ tārāvalī nāma, nandinī maṇibhadrasya /
children.translated_text: When asked by him 'Where is this one from?', she spoke: 'O King! During the past night, a certain divine woman, placing this prince before me, awakening me who was sealed in sleep, spoke respectfully: "O Queen! I am the beloved of <s>Kāmapāla</s>, the son of <s>Dharmapāla</s>, your husband's minister — a <s>Yakṣa</s>-maiden named <s>Tārāvalī</s>, daughter of <s>Maṇibhadra</s> /

children.text: yakṣeśvarānumatyā madātmajametaṃ bhavattanūjasyāmbhonidhivalayaveṣṭitakṣoṇīmaṇḍaleśvarasya bhāvino viśuddhayaśonidhe rājavāhanasya paricaryākaraṇāyānītavatyasmi /
children.translated_text: With the permission of the lord of <s>Yakṣas</s>, I have brought this my son for the service of your son <s>Rājavāhana</s>, who is destined to become lord of the earth-circle encircled by the ocean, a treasury of pure fame /

children.text: tvamenaṃ manojasaṃnibhamabhivardhaya, iti vismayavikasitanayanayā mayā savinayaṃ satkṛtā svakṣī yakṣī sāpyadṛśyatāmayāsīt' iti // Dkc_1,1.73 //
children.translated_text: Nurture him who resembles <s>Manoja</s> (the god of love)." By me, whose eyes widened with wonder, the <s>Yakṣī</s> was respectfully honored, and she too became invisible.' // Dkc_1,1.73 //

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.74:
children.translated_text: START Dkc 1,1.74:

children.text: kāmapālasya yakṣakanyāsaṃgame vismayamānamānaso rājahaṃso rañjitamitraṃ sumitraṃ mantriṇamāhūya tadīyabhrātṛputramarthapālaṃ vidhāya tasmai sarvaṃ vārtādikaṃ vyākhyāyādāt // Dkc_1,1.74 //
children.translated_text: King <s>Rājahaṃsa</s>, his mind filled with wonder at <s>Kāmapāla</s>'s union with the <s>Yakṣa</s>-maiden, summoned the minister <s>Sumitra</s> who had gratified his friends, appointed <s>Arthapāla</s>, the latter's nephew, narrated all the news and so forth to him, and gave [the child] over. // Dkc_1,1.74 //

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.75:
children.translated_text: START Dkc 1,1.75:

children.text: tataḥ parasmin divase vāmadevāntevāsī tadāśramavāsī samārādhitadevakīrtiṃ nirbhartsitamāramūrtiṃ kusumasukumāraṃ kumāramekamavagamayya narapatimavādīt "deva! vilolālakaṃ bālakaṃ nijotsaṅgatale nidhāya rudatīṃ sthavirāmekāṃ vilokyāvocam "sthavire! kā tvam, ayamarbhakaḥ kasya nayanānandakaraḥ kāntāraṃ kimarthamāgatā, śokakāraṇaṃ kim'iti // Dkc_1,1.75 //
children.translated_text: Then, on the following day, a disciple of <s>Vāmadeva</s> dwelling in his hermitage, having brought before the king a single prince — graced with divine fame, having vanquished the form of <s>Māra</s>, soft as flowers — spoke: 'O Lord! Placing a boy with disheveled locks on my lap, seeing an old woman weeping, I asked: "Old woman! Who are you, whose eye-delighting son is this boy, why have you come to the wilderness, what is the cause of your grief?"' // Dkc_1,1.75 //

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.76:
children.translated_text: START Dkc 1,1.76:

children.text:
sā karayugena vāṣpajalamunmṛjya nijaśokaśaṅkūtpāṭanakṣamamiva māmavalokya śokahetumavocat-dvijātmaja! rājahaṃsamantriṇaḥ sitavarmaṇaḥ kanīyānātmajaḥ satyavarmā tīrthayātrāmiṣeṇa deśamenamāgacchat /
sa kasmiṃścidagrahāre kālīṃ nāma kasyacid bhūsurasya nandinīṃ vivāhya tasyā anapatyatayā gaurīṃ nāma tadbhaginīṃ kāñcanakāntiṃ pariṇīya tasyāmekaṃ tanayamalabhata /
kālī sāsūyamekadā dhātryā mayā saha bālamenamekena miṣeṇānīya taṭinyāmetasyāmakṣipat /
children.translated_text: <s>Kālī</s>, one day through jealousy, together with the nurse — that is, me — brought this boy away on some pretext and cast him into this river /

children.text: kareṇaikena bālamuddhṛtyāpareṇa plavamānā nadīvegāgatasya kasyacittaroḥ śākhāmavalambya tatra śiśuṃ nidhāya nadīvegenohyamānā kenacittarulagnena kālabhogināhamadaṃśi /
children.translated_text: Lifting the boy with one hand and swimming with the other, I clung to the branch of a tree that had come with the river's current, placed the child there, and while being carried by the force of the river, I was bitten by a black serpent clinging to some tree /

children.text: madavalambībhūto bhūruho 'yamasmin deśe tīramagamat /
children.translated_text: The tree on which I was clinging came to shore in this region /

children.text: garalasyoddīpanatayā mayi mṛtāyāmaraṇye kaścana śaraṇyo nāstīti mayā śocyate iti // Dkc_1,1.76 //
children.translated_text: I grieve because, as the venom flares up and I die, there is no protector for this child in the forest.' // Dkc_1,1.76 //

She, wiping the stream of tears with both hands, looking at me as if capable of pulling out the thorns of her grief, spoke the cause of her sorrow: 'O son of a twice-born! <s>Satyavarman</s>, the younger son of King <s>Rājahaṃsa</s>'s minister <s>Sitavarman</s>, came to this land on the pretext of a pilgrimage / He, in a certain village, married a woman named <s>Kālī</s>, the daughter of a certain <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, and due to her childlessness, marrying also her sister named <s>Gaurī</s>, of golden beauty, from her he obtained one son /

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.77:
children.translated_text: START Dkc 1,1.77:

children.text: tato viṣamaviṣajvālāvalīḍhāvayavā sā dharaṇītale nyapatat /
children.translated_text: Then she, her limbs licked by the flames of the terrible poison, fell to the ground /

children.text: dayāviṣṭahṛdayo 'haṃ mantrabalena viṣavyathāmapanetumakṣamaḥ samīpakuñjeṣvauṣadhiviśeṣamanviṣya pratyāgato vyutkrāntajīvitāṃ tāṃ vyalokayam // Dkc_1,1.77 //
children.translated_text: I, my heart filled with compassion, unable to remove the pain of the poison by the power of <s>mantras</s>, searched for special herbs in nearby groves and upon returning, beheld her who had departed this life. // Dkc_1,1.77 //

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.78:
children.translated_text: START Dkc 1,1.78:

children.text: tadanu tasyāḥ pāvakasaṃskāraṃ viracya śokākulacetāḥ bālamenamagatimādāya satyavarmavṛttāntavelāyāṃ tannivāsāgrahāranāmadheyasyāśrutatayā tadanveṣaṇamaśakyamityālocya bhavadamātyatanayasya bhavānevābhirakṣiteti bhavantamenamānayam' iti // Dkc_1,1.78 //
children.translated_text: Then, having performed the fire-rite for her, with a heart agitated by grief, taking this helpless boy, at the time of <s>Satyavarman</s>'s story, not having heard the name of the village of his residence, considering that searching for it was impossible, thinking 'Your lordship alone should protect this son of your minister,' I brought him to you.' // Dkc_1,1.78 //

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.79:
children.translated_text: START Dkc 1,1.79:

children.text: tanniśamya satyavarmasthiteḥ samyaganiścitatayā khinnamānaso narapatiḥ sumataye mantriṇe somadattaṃ nāma tadanujatanayamarpitavān /
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the king, his mind distressed by the complete uncertainty of <s>Satyavarman</s>'s situation, entrusted to the minister <s>Sumati</s> the boy, naming him <s>Somadatta</s>, the son of his younger brother /

children.text: so 'pi sodaramāgatamiva manyamāno viśeṣeṇa pupoṣa // Dkc_1,1.79 //
children.translated_text: He (<s>Sumati</s>) too, considering him as if his own brother's son had arrived, nurtured him with special care. // Dkc_1,1.79 //

children.text: START Dkc 1,1.80:
children.translated_text: START Dkc 1,1.80:

children.text: evaṃ militena kumāramaṇḍalena saha bālakelīranubhavannadhirūḍhānekavāhano rājavāhano 'nukrameṇa caulopanayanādisaṃskārajātamalabhata /
children.translated_text: Thus, enjoying childhood play with the assembled circle of princes, <s>Rājavāhana</s>, having mastered many mounts, gradually received the sacraments of tonsure, investiture of the sacred thread, and other rites /

children.text: tataḥ sakalalipijñānaṃ nikhiladeśīyabhāṣāpāṇḍityaṣaḍaṅgasahitavedasamudāyakovidatvaṃ kāvyanāṭakākhyānakākhyāyiketihāsacitrakathāsahitapurāṇagaṇanaipuṇyaṃ dharmaśabdajyotistarkamīmāṃsādi samastaśāstranikaracāturyaṃ kauṭilyakāmandakīyādinītipaṭalakauśalaṃ vīṇādyaśeṣavādyadākṣyaṃ saṃgītasāhityahāritvaṃ maṇimantrauṣadhādimāyāprapañcacuñcutvaṃ mātaṅgaturaṅgādivāhanārohaṇapāṭavaṃ vividhāyudhaprayogacaṇatvaṃ cauryadurodarādikapaṭakalāprauḍhatvaṃ ca tattadācāryebhyaḥ samyaglabdhvā yauvanena vilasantaṃ kumāranikaraṃ nirīkṣya mahīvallabhaḥ saḥ "ahaṃ śatrujanadurlabhaḥ' iti paramānandamamandamavindata // Dkc_1,1.80 //
children.translated_text: Then, having properly acquired from their respective teachers: knowledge of all scripts, mastery of languages of all regions, expertise in the entire collection of <s>Vedas</s> together with the six auxiliary sciences, skill in poetry, drama, tales, fables, histories, wonder-tales, and <s>Purāṇas</s>, dexterity in all the multitude of sciences including <s>Dharma</s>, grammar, astronomy, logic, and <s>Mīmāṃsā</s>, proficiency in the political treatises of <s>Kauṭilya</s>, <s>Kāmandaka</s>, and others, skill in all instruments beginning with the <s>vīṇā</s>, charm in music and literature, cleverness in the arts of illusion involving gems, <s>mantras</s>, and herbs, adroitness in riding elephants, horses, and other mounts, fierceness in the use of various weapons, and proficiency in the deceptive arts of theft and sleight of hand — beholding the group of princes shining with youth, that lord of the earth found supreme, abundant joy, thinking 'I am unassailable by enemies.' // Dkc_1,1.80 //

children.text: iti śrīdaṇḍinaḥ kṛtau daśakumāracarite kumārotpattirnāma prathama ucchvāsaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, in the composition of the illustrious <s>Daṇḍin</s>, in the <s>Daśakumāracarita</s>, [ends] the first chapter named 'The Birth of the Princes.'

children.text: dvitīyocchvāsaḥ
children.translated_text: Second Chapter

children.text: START Dkc 1,2.1:
children.translated_text: START Dkc 1,2.1:

children.text: athaikadā vāmadevaḥ sakalakalākuśalena kusumasāyakasaṃśayitasaundaryeṇa kalpita sodaryeṇa sāhasāpahasitakumāreṇa sukumāreṇa jayadhvajātapavāraṇakuliśāṅkitakareṇa kumāranikareṇa pariveṣṭitaṃ rājānamānataśirasaṃ samabhigamya tena tāṃ kṛtāṃ paricaryāmaṅgīkṛtya nijacaraṇakamalayugalamilanmadhukarāyamāṇakākapakṣaṃ vidaliṣyamāṇavipakṣaṃ kumāracayaṃ gāḍhamāliṅgya mitasatyavākyena vihitāśīrabhyabhāṣata // Dkc_1,2.1 //
children.translated_text: Then one day, <s>Vāmadeva</s> approached the king — who was surrounded by a circle of princes skilled in all arts, whose beauty rivaled that of the Flower-Arrowed one (<s>Kāmadeva</s>), as if specially created brothers, delicate youths who outshone the god of war by their daring, whose hands bore the marks of victory-banner, elephant-goad, and thunderbolt — and bowing his head, having accepted the service they rendered, tightly embracing the group of princes whose side-locks at his lotus-feet resembled hovering bees and who were destined to split asunder their adversaries, spoke blessings in measured, truthful words: // Dkc_1,2.1 //

children.text: START Dkc 1,2.2:
children.translated_text: START Dkc 1,2.2:

children.text: bhūvallabha, bhavadīyamanorathaphalamiva samṛddhalāvaṇyaṃ tāruṇyaṃ nutamitro bhavatputro 'nubhavati /
children.translated_text: 'O lord of the earth, your son enjoys youth rich in beauty, as if the fruit of your heart's desire, with his friend [by his side] /

children.text: sahacarasametasya nūnametasya digvijayārambhasamayaḥ eṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Indeed, for him together with his companions, this is the time to begin the conquest of the directions /

children.text: tadasya sakalakleśasahasya rājavāhanasya digvijayaprayāṇaṃ kriyatām iti // Dkc_1,2.2 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, let the campaign for the conquest of the directions be undertaken for this <s>Rājavāhana</s>, who can endure all hardships.' // Dkc_1,2.2 //

children.text: START Dkc 1,2.3:
children.translated_text: START Dkc 1,2.3:

children.text: kumārā mārābhirāmā rāmādyapauruṣā ruṣā bhasmīkṛtārayo rayopahasitasamīraṇā raṇābhiyānena yānenābhyudayāśaṃsaṃ rājānamakārṣuḥ /
children.translated_text: The princes — charming as <s>Māra</s>, whose valor surpassed <s>Rāma</s> and the others, who had reduced their enemies to ashes with fury, whose speed mocked the wind — by [announcing] their march to battle, filled the king with hope of prosperity /

children.text: tatsācivyamitareṣāṃ vidhāya samucitāṃ buddhimupadiśya śubhe muhūrte saparivāraṃ kumāraṃ vijayāya visasarja // Dkc_1,2.3 //
children.translated_text: Having appointed suitable ministers for the others and imparting appropriate counsel, at an auspicious moment he dispatched the prince with his retinue for victory. // Dkc_1,2.3 //

children.text: START Dkc 1,2.4:
children.translated_text: START Dkc 1,2.4:

children.text: rājavāhano maṅgalasūcakaṃ śubhaśakunaṃ vilokayandeśaṃ kañcidatikramya vindhyāṭavīmadhyamaviśat /
children.translated_text: <s>Rājavāhana</s>, observing auspicious omens heralding good fortune, crossed a certain territory and entered the midst of the <s>Vindhya</s> forest /

children.text: tatra hetihatikiṇāṅkaṃ kālāyasakarkaśakāyaṃ yajñopavītenānumeyaviprabhāvaṃ vyaktakirātaprabhāvaṃ locanaparuṣaṃ kamapi puruṣaṃ dadarśa // Dkc_1,2.4 //
children.translated_text: There he saw a certain man, his body scarred with weapon-wounds, hard as dark iron, whose <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> status was inferred from the sacred thread on his shoulder, yet whose demeanor was clearly that of a <s>Kirāta</s> (forest-tribesman), with fierce eyes. // Dkc_1,2.4 //

children.text: START Dkc 1,2.5:
children.translated_text: START Dkc 1,2.5:

children.text: tena vihitapūjano rājavāhano 'bhāṣata-"nanu mānava, janasaṅgarahite mṛgahite ghorapracāre kāntāre vindhyāṭavīmadhye bhavānekākī kimiti nivasati /
children.translated_text: Having been honored by him, <s>Rājavāhana</s> spoke: 'Indeed, O man, in this fearsome wilderness devoid of people, frequented by wild beasts, in the midst of the <s>Vindhya</s> forest — why do you dwell here alone? /

children.text: bhavadaṃsopanītaṃ yajñopavītaṃ bhūsurabhāvaṃ dyotayati /
children.translated_text: The sacred thread placed upon your shoulder indicates <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> status /

children.text: hetihatibhiḥ kirātarītiranumīyate /
children.translated_text: From the scars of weapons, the ways of a <s>Kirāta</s> are inferred /

children.text: kathaya kimetat' iti // Dkc_1,2.5 //
children.translated_text: Tell me, what is the meaning of this?' // Dkc_1,2.5 //

children.text: START Dkc 1,2.6:
children.translated_text: START Dkc 1,2.6:

children.text: `tejomayo 'yaṃ mānuṣamātrapauruṣo nūnaṃ na bhavati' iti matvā sa puruṣastadvayasya mukhānnāmajanane vijñāya tasmai nijavṛttāntamakathayat-"rājanandana, kecidasyāmaṭavyāṃ vedādividyābhyāsamapahāya nijakulācāraṃ dūrīkṛtya satyaśaucādidharmavrātaṃ parihṛtya kilviṣamanviṣyantaḥ pulindapurogamāstadannamupabhuñjānābahavo brāhmaṇabruvā nivasanti teṣu kasyacitputro nindāpātracāritro mātaṅgonāmāhaṃ sahakirātabalena janapadaṃ praviśya grāmeṣu dhaninaḥ strībālasahitānānīyāṭavyāṃ bandhane nidhāya teṣāṃ sakaladhanamapaharannuddhato vītadayo vyacaram /
children.translated_text: Thinking 'This radiant one is surely not of merely human prowess,' that man, having learned from the retinue's lips the names and lineage [of the prince], narrated to him his own story: 'O prince, in this forest there dwell many <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>-in-name-only who, abandoning the study of the <s>Vedas</s> and other sciences, casting off their family traditions, discarding the multitude of duties such as truthfulness and purity, and seeking sin — led by <s>Pulindas</s> (forest-tribes), subsisting on their food. Among them I am the son of one, a man of shameful conduct named <s>Mātaṅga</s>, who with a force of <s>Kirātas</s>, entering the countryside, carrying off wealthy householders together with their women and children from the villages, imprisoning them in the forest, and seizing all their wealth, used to roam about arrogant and devoid of compassion /

children.text: kadācidekasmin kāntāre madīyasahacaragaṇena jighāṃsyamānaṃ bhūsuramekamavalokya dayāyattacitto 'bravam-"nanu pāpāḥ, na hantavyo brāhmaṇa' iti // Dkc_1,2.6 //
START Dkc 1,2.7:
te roṣāruṇanayanā māṃ bahudhā nirabhartsayan /
teṣāṃ bhāṣaṇapāruṣyamasahiṣṇurahamavanisurarakṣaṇāya ciraṃ prayudhya tairabhihato gatajīvito 'bhavam // Dkc_1,2.7 //
START Dkc 1,2.8:
tataḥ pretapurīmupetya tatra dehadhāribhiḥ puruṣaiḥ pariveṣṭitaṃ sabhāmadhye ratnakhacitasiṃhāsanāsīnaṃ śamanaṃ vilokya tasmai daṇḍapraṇāmamakaravam /
so 'pi māmavekṣya citraguptaṃ nāma nijāmātyamāhūya tamavocat "saciva, naiṣo 'muṣya mṛtyusamayaḥ /
ninditacarito 'pyayaṃ mahīsuranimittaṃ gatajīvito 'bhūt /
itaḥprabhṛti vigalitakalmaṣasyāsya puṇyakarmakaraṇe rucirudeṣyati /
pāpiṣṭhairanubhūyamānamatra yātanāviśeṣaṃ vilokya punarapi pūrvaśarīramanena gamyatām' iti // Dkc_1,2.8 //
START Dkc 1,2.9:

citragupto 'pi tatra tatra santapteṣvāyasastambheṣu badhyamānān, atyuṣṇīkṛte vitataśarāve taile nikṣipyamāṇān, laguḍairjarjarīkṛtāvayavān, niśitaṭaṅkaiḥ paritakṣyamāṇānapi darśayitvā puṇyabuddhimupadiśya māmamuñcat /
tadeva pūrvaśarīramahaṃ prāpto mahāṭavīmadhye śītalopacāraṃ racayatā mahīsureṇa parīkṣyamāṇaḥ śilāyāṃ śayitaḥ kṣaṇamatiṣṭham // Dkc_1,2.9 //
START Dkc 1,2.10:
tadanu viditodanto madīyavaṃśabandhugaṇaḥ sahasāgatya mandiramānīya māmapakrāntavraṇamakarot /

dvijanmā kṛtajño mahyamakṣaraśikṣāṃ vidhāya vividhāgamatantramākhyāya kalmaṣakṣayakāraṇaṃ sadācāramupadiśya jñānekṣaṇagamyamānasya śaśikhaṇḍaśekharasya pūjāvidhānamabhidhāya pūjāṃ matkṛtāmaṅgīkṛtya niragāt // Dkc_1,2.10 //
START Dkc 1,2.11:
tadārabhyāhaṃ kirātakṛtasaṃsargaṃ bandhuvargamutsṛjya sakalalokaikagurumindukalāvataṃsaṃ cetasi smarannasminkānane dūrīkṛtakalaṅko vasāmi /
"deva, bhavate vijñāpanīyaṃ rahasyaṃ kiñcidasti /
āgamyatām iti // Dkc_1,2.11 //
START Dkc 1,2.12:

sa vayasyagaṇādapanīya rahasi punarenamabhāṣata-"rājan, atīte niśānte gaurīpatiḥ svapnasannihito nidrāmudritalocanaṃ vibodhya prasannavadanakāntiḥ praśrayānataṃ māmavocat-mātaṅga, daṇḍakāraṇyāntarālagāminyāstaṭinyāstīrabhūmau siddhasādhyārādhyamānasya sphaṭikaliṅgasya paścādadripatikanyāpadapaṅkticihnitasyāśmanaḥ savidhe vidherānanamiva kimapi bilaṃ vidyate /
tatpraviśya tatra nikṣiptaṃ tāmraśāsanaṃ śāsanaṃ vidhāturiva samādāya vidhiṃ tadupadiṣṭaṃ diṣṭavijayamiva vidhāya pātālalokādhīśvareṇa bhavatā bhavitavyam /
bhavatsāhāyyakaro rājakumāro 'dya śvo vā samāgamiṣyati' iti /
tadādeśānuguṇameva bhavadāgamanamabhūt /
sādhanābhilāṣiṇo mama toṣiṇo racaya sāhāyyam' iti // Dkc_1,2.12 //
START Dkc 1,2.13:
`tathā' iti rājavāhanaḥ sākaṃ mātaṅgena namitottamāṅgena vihāyārdharātre nidrāparatantraṃ mitragaṇaṃ vanāntaramavāpa /

tadanu tadanucarāḥ kalyena sākalye rājakumāramanavalokayanto viṣaṇṇahṛdayāsteṣu teṣu vaneṣu samyaganviṣyānavekṣamāṇā etadanveṣaṇamanīṣayā deśāntaraṃ cariṣṇavo 'tisahiṣṇavo niścitapunaḥsaṃketasthānāḥ parasparaṃ viyujya yayuḥ // Dkc_1,2.13 //
START Dkc 1,2.14:

lokaikavīreṇa kumāreṇa rakṣyamāṇaḥ santuṣṭāntaraṅgo mātaṅgo 'pi bilaṃ śaśiśekharakathitābhijñānaparijñātaṃ niḥśaṅkaṃ praviśya gṛhītatāmraśāsano rasātalaṃ pathā tenaivopetya tatra kasyacitpattanasya nikaṭe kelīkānanakāsārasya vitatasārasasya samīpe nānāvidheneśaśāsanavidhānopapāditena haviṣā homaṃ viracya pratyūhaparihāriṇi savismayaṃ vilokayati rājavāhane samidhājyasamujjvalite jvalane puṇyagehaṃ dehaṃ mantrapūrvakamāhutīkṛtya taḍitsamānakāntiṃ divyāṃ tanumalabhata // Dkc_1,2.14 //
START Dkc 1,2.15:

tadanu maṇimayamaṇḍanamaṇḍalamaṇḍitā sakalalokalalanākulalalāmabhūtā kanyakā kācana vinītānekasakhījanānugamyamānā kalahaṃsagatyā śanairāgatyāvanisurottamāya maṇimekamujjvalākāramupāyanīkṛtya tena "kā tvam' iti pṛṣṭā sotkaṇṭhā kalakaṇṭhasvanena mandaṃ mandamudañjalirabhāṣata // Dkc_1,2.15 //
START Dkc 1,2.16:
`bhūsurottama, ahamasurottamanandinī kālindī nāma /
mama pitāsya lokasya śāsitā mahānubhāvo nijaparākramāsahiṣṇunā viṣṇunā dūrīkṛtāmare samare yamanagarātithirakāri /
tadviyogaśokasāgaramagnāṃ māmavekṣya ko 'pi kāruṇikaḥ siddhatāpaso 'bhāṣata // Dkc_1,2.16 //
START Dkc 1,2.17:
`bāle, kaściddivyadehadhārī mānavo navo vallabhastava bhūtvā sakalaṃ rasātalaṃ pālayiṣyati' iti /
tadādeśaṃ niśamya ghanaśabdonmukhī cātakī varṣāgamanamiva tavālokanakāṅkṣiṇī ciramatiṣṭham /
manmanorathaphalāyamānaṃ bhavadāgamanamavagamya madrājyāvalambabhūtāmātyānumatyā madanakṛtasārathyena manasā bhavantamāgaccham /
lokasyāsya rājalakṣmīmaṅgīkṛtya māṃ tatsapatnīṃ karotu bhavān' iti // Dkc_1,2.17 //
START Dkc 1,2.18:
mātaṅgo 'pi rājavāhanānumatyā tāṃ taruṇīṃ pariṇīya divyāṅganālābhena hṛṣṭataro rasātalarājyamurarīkṛtya paramānandamāsasāda // Dkc_1,2.18 //
START Dkc 1,2.19:

vañcayitvā vayasyagaṇaṃ samāgato rājavāhanastadavalokanakautūhalena bhuvaṃ gamiṣṇuḥ kālindīdattaṃ kṣutpipāsādikleśanāśanaṃ maṇiṃ sāhāyyakaraṇasantuṣṭānmataṅgāllabdhvā kañcanādhvānamanuvartamānaṃ taṃ visṛjya bilapathena tena niryayau /
tatra ca mitragaṇamavalokya bhuvaṃ babhrāma // Dkc_1,2.19 //
START Dkc 1,2.20:
bhramaṃśca viśālopaśalye kamapyākrīḍamāsādya tatra viśaśramiṣurāndolikārūḍhaṃ ramaṇīsahitamāptajanaparivṛtamudyāne samāgatamekaṃ puruṣamapaśyat /
so 'pi paramānandena pallavitacetā vikasitavadanāravindaḥ "mama svāmī somakulāvataṃso viśuddhayaśonidhī rājavāhanaḥ eṣaḥ /
mahābhāgyatayākāṇḍa evāsya pādamūlaṃ gatavānasmi /

samprati mahānnayanotsavo jātaḥ' iti sasaṃbhramamāndolikāyā avatīrya sarabhasapadavinyāsavilāsiharṣotkarṣacaritastricaturapadānyudgatasya caraṇakamalayugalaṃ galadullasanmallikāvalayena maulinā pasparśa // Dkc_1,2.20 //
START Dkc 1,2.21:
pramodāśrupūrṇo rājā pulakitāṅgaṃ taṃ gāḍhamāliṅgya "aye saumya somadatta!' iti vyājahāra /

tataḥ kasyāpi punnāgabhūruhasya chāyāśītale tale saṃviṣṭena manujanāthena sapraṇayamabhāṇi-"sakhe! kālametāvantaṃ, deśe kasmin, prakāreṇa kenāsthāyi bhavatā, saṃprati kutra gamyate, taruṇī keyaṃ, eṣa parijanaḥ sampāditaḥ kathaṃ, kathaya iti // Dkc_1,2.21 //
START Dkc 1,2.22:
so 'pi mitrasaṃdarśanavyatikarāpagatacintājvarātiśayo mukulitakarakamalaḥ savinayamātmīyapracāraprakāramavocat // Dkc_1,2.22 //
iti śrīdaṇḍinaḥ kṛtau daśakumāracarite dvijopakṛtirnāma dvitīya ucchvāsaḥ
tṛtīyocchvāsaḥ
START Dkc 1,3.1:
`deva, bhavaccaraṇakamalasevābhilāṣībhūto 'haṃ bhramannekasyāṃ vanāvanau pipāsākulo latāparivṛtaṃ śītalaṃ nadasalilaṃ pibannujjvalākāraṃ ratnaṃ tatraikamadrākṣam /
children.translated_text: 'O lord, I, desirous of serving Your Lordship's lotus-feet, was wandering about. In a certain forest glade, parched with thirst, while drinking cool river water surrounded by creepers, I beheld therein a single gem of brilliant appearance.

children.text: tadādāya gatvā kañcanādhvānamambaramaṇeratyuṣṇatayā gantumakṣamo vane 'sminneva kimapi devatāyatanaṃ praviṣṭo dīnānanaṃ bahutanayasametaṃ sthaviramahīsuramekamavalokya kuśalamuditadayo 'hamapṛccham // Dkc_1,3.1 //
children.translated_text: Taking it and proceeding along a golden road, unable to travel further due to the excessive heat of the sun, I entered some temple of a deity in this very forest. Seeing there an old <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> with a dejected face, accompanied by many children, I, filled with compassion, asked about his well-being. // Dkc 1.3.1 //

children.text: START Dkc 1,3.2:
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Dkc 1.3.2:]

children.text: kārpaṇyavivarṇavadano madāśāpūrṇamānaso 'vocadagrajanmā-"mahābhāga sutānetānmātṛhīnānanekairupāyai rakṣannidānīmasminkudeśe bhaikṣyaṃ saṃpādya dadadetebhyo vasāmi śivālaye 'smin'iti // Dkc_1,3.2 //
children.translated_text: The twice-born one, his face pale with wretchedness, his mind full of hope at my generosity, spoke: "O fortunate one, protecting these motherless children of mine by various means, I now live in this <s>Śiva</s>-temple in this wretched place, procuring alms and giving [them] to these [children]." // Dkc 1.3.2 //

children.text: START Dkc 1,3.3:
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Dkc 1.3.3:]

children.text: `bhūdeva, etatkaṭakādhipatī rājā kasya deśasya, kiṃ nāmadheyaḥ, kimatrāgamanakāraṇamasya' iti pṛṣṭo 'bhāṣata mahīsuraḥ-"saumya, mattakālo nāma lāṭeśvaro deśasyāsya pālayiturvīraketostanayāṃ vāmalocanāṃ nāma taruṇīratnamasamānalāvaṇyāṃ śrāvaṃ śrāvamavadhūtaduhitṛprārthanasya tasya nagarīmarautsīt /
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, who is the lord of this encampment? King of which land? What is his name? What is the reason for his coming here?' — thus questioned, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> said: "Friend, the one named <s>Mattakāla</s>, lord of the <s>Lāṭa</s> country, hearing of the daughter of <s>Vīraketu</s>, the protector of this land — a jewel of a young woman named <s>Vāmalocanā</s>, of incomparable beauty — hearing again and again, he whose requests for the daughter had been rejected, attacked [<s>Vīraketu</s>'s] capital city.

children.text: vīraketurapi bhīto mahadupāyanamiva tanayāṃ mattakālāyādāt /
children.translated_text: <s>Vīraketu</s> too, frightened, gave [his] daughter to <s>Mattakāla</s> as if [she were] a great tribute.

children.text: taruṇīlābhahṛṣṭacetā lāṭapatiḥ "pariṇeyā nijapura eva' iti niścitya gacchannijadeśaṃ prati saṃprati mṛgayādareṇātra vane sainyāvāsamakārayat // Dkc_1,3.3 //
children.translated_text: The lord of <s>Lāṭa</s>, his heart delighted at obtaining the young woman, deciding 'I shall marry [her] in my own city,' and [now] going toward his own land, has presently, out of fondness for hunting, set up a military encampment here in the forest." // Dkc 1.3.3 //

children.text: START Dkc 1,3.4:
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Dkc 1.3.4:]

children.text: kanyāsāreṇa niyukto mānapālo nāma vīraketumantrī mānadhanaścturaṅgabala samanvito 'nyatra racitaśibirastaṃ nijanāthāvamānakhinnamānaso 'ntarbibheda iti // Dkc_1,3.4 //
children.translated_text: The minister of <s>Vīraketu</s> named <s>Mānapāla</s>, assigned to the escort of the princess, proud and wealthy, accompanied by cavalry, had pitched his camp elsewhere, his spirit broken by the humiliation of his own lord, and [he] harbored inner rebellion. // Dkc 1.3.4 //

children.text: START Dkc 1,3.5:
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Dkc 1.3.5:]

children.text: vipro 'sau bahutanayo vidvānnirdhanaḥ sthaviraśca dānayogya iti tasmai karuṇāpūrṇamanā ratnamadām /
children.translated_text: That <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> was [a man of] many children, learned, destitute, and elderly — [thus] worthy of charity. To him, my heart filled with compassion, I gave the gem.

children.text: paramāhlādavikasitānano 'bhihitānekāśīḥ kutracidagrajanmā jagāma /
children.translated_text: His face blossoming with supreme delight, having uttered many blessings, the twice-born one went somewhere.

children.text: adhvaśramakhinnena mayā tatra niraveśi nidrāsukham /
children.translated_text: Weary from travel, I settled there and enjoyed the pleasure of sleep.

children.text: tadanu paścānnigaḍitabāhuyugalaḥ sa bhūsuraḥ kaśāghātacihnitagātro 'nekanaistriṃśikānuyāto 'bhyetya mām "asau dasyuḥ' ityadarśayat // Dkc_1,3.5 //
children.translated_text: Thereupon, that very <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, his arms bound in chains, his body marked by whip-blows, accompanied by many swordsmen, approached and pointed me out [saying] 'This is the thief!' // Dkc 1.3.5 //

children.text: START Dkc 1,3.6:
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Dkc 1.3.6:]

children.text: parityaktabhūsurā rājabhaṭā ratnāvāptiprakāraṃ maduktamanākarṇya bhayarahitaṃ māṃ gāḍhaṃ niyamya rajjubhirānīya kārāgāram "ete tava sakhāyaḥ' iti nigaḍitānkāṃścinnirdiṣṭavanto māmapi nigaḍitacaraṇayugalamakārṣuḥ /
