children.translated_text: The royal soldiers, having set the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> free, without hearing the manner of my obtaining the gem as told by me, fearlessly seizing me tightly and binding me with ropes, brought me to the prison. 'These are your companions,' they said, pointing to certain [men] who were [already] chained, and chained my two feet as well.

children.text: kiḍkartavyatāmūḍhena nirāśakleśānubhavenāvāci mayā-"nanu puruṣā vīryaparuṣāḥ, nimittena kena niviśatha kārāvāsaduḥkhaṃ dustaram /
children.translated_text: Bewildered as to what should be done, experiencing the anguish of hopelessness, I said: 'Surely you are men, fierce in valor! For what reason do you endure this unbearable suffering of imprisonment?

children.text: yūyaṃ vayasyā iti nirdiṣṭametaiḥ, kimidam iti // Dkc_1,3.6 //
children.translated_text: You have been identified by these [soldiers] as [my] companions — what is this about?' // Dkc 1.3.6 //

children.text: START Dkc 1,3.7:
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Dkc 1.3.7:]

children.text: tathāvidhaṃ māmavekṣya bhūsurānmayā śrutaṃ lāṭapativṛttāntaṃ vyākhyāya coravīrāḥ punaravocan-"mahābhāga! vīraketumantriṇo mānapālasya kiṅkarā vayam /
children.translated_text: Seeing me in such a state, the heroic robbers, having narrated the circumstances of the lord of <s>Lāṭa</s> that I had heard from the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, then said: 'O fortunate one! We are the servants of <s>Mānapāla</s>, the minister of <s>Vīraketu</s>.

children.text: tadājñayā lāṭeśvaramāraṇāya rātrau suraṅgadvāreṇa tadagāraṃ praviśya tatra rājābhāvena viṣaṇṇā bahudhanamāhṛtya mahāṭavīṃ prāviśāma /
children.translated_text: By his command, in order to kill the lord of <s>Lāṭa</s>, we entered his quarters at night through a secret tunnel; but, finding the king absent there, being despondent, we seized much wealth and entered the great forest.

children.text: aparedyuśca padānveṣiṇo rājānucarā bahavo 'bhyetya dhṛtadhanacayānasmānparitaḥ parivṛtya dṛḍhataraṃ baddhvā nikaṭamānīya samastavastuśodhanavelāyāmekasyānarghyaratnasyābhāvenāsmadvadhāya māṇikyādānādasmān kilāśṛṅkhalayan iti // Dkc_1,3.7 //
children.translated_text: The next day, the king's followers, tracking our footprints, came in large numbers, surrounded us who held the plundered wealth, bound us extremely tightly, brought us near, and at the time of searching all the goods, because of the absence of a single priceless gem, they chained us — supposedly for the theft of the ruby — for our execution.' // Dkc 1.3.7 //

children.text: START Dkc 1,3.8:
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Dkc 1.3.8:]

children.text: śrutaratnaratnāvalokasthāno 'ham "idaṃ tadeva māṇikyam' iti niścitya bhūdevadānanimittāṃ duravasthāmātmano janma nāmadheyaṃ yuṣmadanveṣaṇaparyaṭanaprakāraṃ cābhāṣya samayocitaiḥ saṃlāpairmaitrīmakārṣam /
children.translated_text: I, who had become [one in] a position to behold the gem of which I had heard, ascertaining 'this is that very ruby,' explained to them the unfortunate situation resulting from my gift to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, my birth, my name, the manner of my wandering in search of you all, and by timely conversation, I formed a friendship [with them].

children.text: tator'dharātre teṣāṃ mama ca śṛṅkhalābandhanaṃ nirbhidya tairanugamyamāno nidritasya dvāḥsthagaṇasyāyudhajālamādāya purarakṣānpurato 'bhimukhāgatānpaṭuparākramalīlayābhidrāvya mānapālaśibiraṃ prāviśam /
children.translated_text: Then, at midnight, breaking the chains that bound them and me, followed by them, seizing the weapons of the sleeping gatekeepers, I attacked and put to flight with displays of vigorous prowess the city guards who came rushing forward, and entered the camp of <s>Mānapāla</s>.

children.text: mānapālo nijakiṅkarebhyo mama kulābhimānavṛttāntaṃ tatkālīnaṃ vikramaṃ ca niśamya māmārcayat // Dkc_1,3.8 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mānapāla</s>, having heard from his own servants the account of my noble lineage and my valor at that time, honored me. // Dkc 1.3.8 //

children.text: START Dkc 1,3.9:
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Dkc 1.3.9:]

children.text:
paredyurmattakālena preṣitāḥ kecana puruṣā mānapālamupetya "mantrin, madīyarājamandire suraṅgayā bahudhanamapahṛtya coravīrā bhavadīyaṃ kaṭakaṃ prāviśan tānarpaya /
no cenmahānanarthaḥ bhaviṣyati iti krūrataraṃ vākyamabruvan /
tadākarṇya roṣāruṇitanetro mantrī lāṭapatiḥ kaḥ, tena maitrī kā, punarasya varākasya sevayā kiṃ labhyam iti tānnirabhartsayat, te ca mānapālenoktaṃ vipralāpaṃ mattakālāya tathaivākathayan /
kupito 'pi lāṭapatirdervīryagarveṇālpasainikasameto yoddhumabhyagāt /
children.translated_text: Though enraged, the lord of <s>Lāṭa</s>, proud of his wicked valor, advanced to fight with only a small force.

children.text: pūrvameva kṛtaraṇaniścayo mānī mānapālaḥ saṃnaddhayodho yuddhakāmo bhūtvā niḥśaṅkaṃ niragāt /
children.translated_text: The proud <s>Mānapāla</s>, who had already resolved upon battle, his warriors armed, desirous of war, marched out without hesitation.

children.text: ahamapi sabahumānaṃ mantridattāni bahulaturaṅgamopetaṃ caturasārathiṃ rathaṃ dṛḍhataraṃ kavacaṃ madanurūpaṃ cāpaṃ ca vividhabāṇapūrṇaṃ tūṇīradvayaṃ raṇasamucitānyāyudhāni gṛhītvā yuddhasaṃnaddho madīyabalaviśvāsena ripūddharaṇodyuktaṃ mantriṇamanvagām /
children.translated_text: I too, respectfully receiving from the minister a chariot equipped with many horses and a skilled charioteer, a sturdy suit of armor, a bow suited to my strength, two quivers filled with various arrows, and weapons appropriate for battle, armed for war and trusting in my own strength, followed the minister who was eager to uproot the enemy.

children.text: parasparamatsareṇa tumulasaṅgarakaramubhayasainyamatikramya samullasadbhujāṭopena bāṇavarṣaṃ tadaṅge vimuñcannarātīn prāharam // Dkc_1,3.9 //
children.translated_text: Surpassing both armies that clashed in a tumultuous battle through mutual rivalry, displaying the might of my upraised arms, I struck the enemies, releasing a shower of arrows upon their ranks. // Dkc 1.3.9 //

The next day, certain men sent by <s>Mattakāla</s>, approaching <s>Mānapāla</s>, spoke most cruelly: 'O minister, heroic thieves entered my royal palace through a tunnel and stole much wealth, then entered your encampment. Hand them over!
Otherwise, great calamity will befall [you]!'
Hearing that, the minister, his eyes reddened with anger, [said:] 'Who is this lord of <s>Lāṭa</s>? What friendship [have we] with him? What can be gained from the service of that wretch?' — and rebuked them. They reported <s>Mānapāla</s>'s insolent speech to <s>Mattakāla</s> exactly as it was.

children.text: START Dkc 1,3.10:
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Dkc 1.3.10:]

children.text: tato 'tirayaturaṅgamaṃ madrathaṃ tannikaṭaṃ nītvā śīghralaṅghanopetatadīyaratho 'hamarāteḥ śiraḥkartanamakārṣam /
children.translated_text: Then, driving my chariot — [drawn by] exceedingly swift horses — close to him, I, whose own chariot was equipped for rapid leaping, severed the head of the enemy.

children.text: tasminpatite tadavaśiṣṭasainikeṣu palāyiteṣu nānāvidhahayagajādivastujātamādāya paramānandasaṃbhṛto mantrī mamānekavidhāṃ saṃbhāvanāmakārṣīt // Dkc_1,3.10 //
children.translated_text: When he fell and his remaining soldiers fled, the minister, having seized various kinds of horses, elephants, and other goods, filled with supreme joy, bestowed upon me manifold honors. // Dkc 1.3.10 //

children.text: START Dkc 1,3.11:
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Dkc 1.3.11:]

children.text: mānapālapreṣitāttadanucarādenamakhilamudantajātamākarṇya santuṣṭamanā rājābhyudgato madīyaparākrame vismayamānaḥ samahotsavamamātyabāndhavānumatyā śubhadine nijatanayāṃ mahyamadāt /
children.translated_text: Thereupon, King [<s>Vīraketu</s>], having heard the entire account from a follower of <s>Mānapāla</s> sent [for that purpose], his mind content, came forward to meet [us], marveling at my valor, and with great celebration, with the approval of his ministers and kinsmen, on an auspicious day, gave his own daughter to me.

children.text: tato yauvarājyābhiṣikto 'hamanudinamārādhitamahīpālacitto vāmalocanayānayā saha nānāvidhaṃ saukhyamanubhavanbhavadvirahavedanāśalyasulabhavaikalyahṛdayaḥ siddhādeśena suhṛjjanāvalokanaphalaṃ pradeśaṃ mahākālanivāsinaḥ parameśvarasyārādhanāyādya patnīsametaḥ samāgato 'smi /
children.translated_text: Then, anointed as heir-apparent, I, day by day winning the heart of the king, enjoying various pleasures with this [lady] <s>Vāmalocanā</s>, yet with a heart easily afflicted by the thorn of the pain of separation from you all — by the instruction of a <s>Siddha</s>, [I went to] a place that yields the fruit of beholding dear friends, and have today arrived with my wife for the worship of the supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>) dwelling at <s>Mahākāla</s>.

children.text: bhaktavatsalasya gaurīpateḥ kāruṇyena tvatpadāravindasaṃdarśanānandasaṃdoho mayā labdhaḥ' iti // Dkc_1,3.11 //
children.translated_text: Through the compassion of the Lord of <s>Gaurī</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), who is tender toward his devotees, I have obtained the flood of joy of beholding your lotus-feet.' // Dkc 1.3.11 //

children.text: START Dkc 1,3.12:
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Dkc 1.3.12:]

children.text: tanniśamyābhinanditaparākramo rājavāhanastanniraparādhadaṇḍe daivamupālabhya tasmai krameṇātmacaritaṃ kathayāmāsa /
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Rājavāhana</s>, having praised his valor, blaming fate for his blameless punishment, then narrated to him his own adventures in order.

children.text: tasminnavasare purataḥ puṣpodbhavaṃ vilokya sasaṃbhramaṃ nijaniṭilataṭaspṛṣṭacaraṇāṅgulimudañjalimamuṃ gāḍhamāliṅgyānandabāṣpasaṃkulasaṃphullalocanaḥ "saumya somadatta, ayaṃ saḥ puṣpodbhavaḥ' iti tasmai taṃ darśayāmāsa // Dkc_1,3.12 //
children.translated_text: At that moment, seeing <s>Puṣpodbhava</s> before [him], he [<s>Rājavāhana</s>], with agitation, his fingertips touching his own forehead, raising his joined palms, embracing him tightly, his wide-open eyes brimming with tears of joy, said: 'Dear <s>Somadatta</s>, this is that <s>Puṣpodbhava</s>!' — and showed him [to <s>Somadatta</s>]. // Dkc 1.3.12 //

children.text: START Dkc 1,3.13:
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Dkc 1.3.13:]

children.text: tau ca ciravirahaduḥkhaṃ visṛjyānyonyāliṅganasukhamanvabhūtām /
tatastasyaiva mahīruhasya chāyāyāmupaviśya rājā sādarahāsamabhāṣata-"vayasya, bhūsurakāryaṃ kariṣṇurahaṃ mitragaṇo viditārthaḥ sarvathāntarāyaṃ kariṣyatīti nidritānbhavataḥ parityajya niragām /
children.translated_text: Then, sitting in the shade of that very tree, the king said with a respectful smile: 'Friend, I, about to perform the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s rite, [left because] I realized that the group of friends, knowing the purpose, would in every way create an obstacle — so I departed, leaving you all asleep.

children.text: tadanu prabuddho vayasyavargaḥ kimiti niścitya madanveṣaṇāya kutra gatavān /
children.translated_text: Afterward, when the group of friends awoke, having decided 'why [did he leave]?' — where did they go in search of me?

children.text: bhavānekākī kutra gataḥ' iti /
children.translated_text: Where did you go alone?'

children.text: so 'pi lalāṭataṭacumbadañjalipuṭaḥ savinayamalapat // Dkc_1,3.13 //
children.translated_text: He [<s>Somadatta</s>] too, with his joined palms touching his forehead, spoke humbly. // Dkc 1.3.13 //
And those two, casting off the sorrow of long separation, experienced the joy of mutual embrace.

children.text: iti śrīdaṇḍinaḥ kṛtau daśakumāracarite somadattacaritaṃ nāma tṛtīya ucchvāsaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, in the composition of the illustrious <s>Daṇḍin</s>, in the <s>Daśakumāracarita</s>, [this is] the third chapter (<s>ucchvāsa</s>), named the Adventures of <s>Somadatta</s>.

children.text: caturthocchvāsaḥ
children.translated_text: Fourth chapter (<s>ucchvāsa</s>)

children.text: START Dkc 1,4.1:
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Dkc 1.4.1:]

children.text: `deva, mahīsuropakārāyaiva devo gatavāniti niścityāpi devena gantavyaṃ deśaṃ nirṇetu maśaknuvāno mitragaṇaḥ parasparaṃ viyujya dikṣu devamanveṣṭumagacchat // Dkc_1,4.1 //
children.translated_text: 'O Lord, even though the band of friends determined that the lord had gone for the benefit of the earth-dwellers, unable to ascertain the region to which the lord had gone, they separated from one another and went in all directions to search for the lord.' (Dkc 1,4.1)

children.text: START Dkc 1,4.2:
children.translated_text: START Dkc 1,4.2:

children.text: ahamapi devasyānveṣaṇāya mahīmaṭankadācidambaramadhyagatasyāmbaramaṇeḥ kiraṇamasahiṣṇurekasya giritaṭamahīruhasya pracchāyaśītale tale kṣaṇamupāviśam /
children.translated_text: I too, while wandering the earth in search of the lord, once unable to bear the rays of the sun stationed in the middle of the sky, sat down for a moment on the cool ground shaded by a tree on a mountainside.

children.text: mama purobhāge dinamadhyasaṃkucitasarvāvayavāṃ kūrmākṛtiṃ mānuṣacchāyāṃ nirīkṣyonmukho gaganatalānmahārayeṇa patantaṃ puruṣaṃ kañcidantarāla eva dayopanatahṛdayo 'hamavalambya śanairavanitale nikṣipya dūrāpātavītasaṃjñaṃ taṃ śiśiropacāreṇa vibodhya śokātirekeṇodgatabāṣpalocanaṃ taṃ bhṛgupatanakāraṇamapṛccham // Dkc_1,4.2 //
children.translated_text: Before me, observing a human shadow with all limbs contracted at midday in the shape of a tortoise, I looked up, and seeing some man falling from the vault of the sky with great force, I, with compassion arising in my heart, caught him in mid-air, gently placed him on the ground, revived him — who had lost consciousness from the long fall — with cool remedies, and asked him, whose eyes were overflowing with tears from excess of grief, the reason for his plunge from the cliff. (Dkc 1,4.2)

children.text: START Dkc 1,4.3:
children.translated_text: START Dkc 1,4.3:

children.text: so 'pi kararuhairaśrukaṇānapanayannabhāṣata--"saumya, magadhādhināthāmātyasya padmodbhavasyātmasaṃbhavo ratnodbhavo nāmāham /
children.translated_text: He too, wiping away the teardrops with his fingernails, spoke: 'Friend, I am named <s>Ratnodbhava</s>, born of <s>Padmodbhava</s>, a minister of the lord of <s>Magadha</s>.

children.text: vāṇijyarūpeṇa kālayavanadvīpamupetya kāmapi vaṇikkanyakāṃ pariṇīya tayā saha pratyāgacchannambudhau tīrasyānatidūra eva pravahaṇasya bhagnatayā sarveṣu nimagneṣu kathaṅkathamapi daivānukūlyena tīrabhūmimabhigamya nijāṅganāviyogaduḥkhārṇave plavamānaḥ kasyāpi siddhatāpasasyādeśādareṇa ṣoḍaśa hāyanāni kathañcinnītvā duḥkhasya pāramanavekṣamāṇaḥ giripatanamakārṣam' iti // Dkc_1,4.3 //
children.translated_text: Having gone to the island of <s>Kālayavana</s> in the guise of a merchant, I married a certain merchant's daughter and was returning with her when, not very far from the shore, the ship broke apart in the ocean. When all were drowned, somehow by the favor of destiny I reached the shore, and floating in an ocean of grief at the separation from my wife, by the instruction of some accomplished ascetic, with effort I passed sixteen years, and seeing no end to my suffering, I threw myself from the mountain.' (Dkc 1,4.3)

children.text: START Dkc 1,4.4:
children.translated_text: START Dkc 1,4.4:

children.text: tasminnevāvasare kimapi nārīkūjitamaśrāvi-"nakhalu samucitamidaṃ yatsiddhādiṣṭe patitatanayamilane virahamasahiṣṇurvaiśvānaraṃ viśasi' iti // Dkc_1,4.4 //
children.translated_text: At that very moment, some woman's voice was heard: 'It is not fitting that, when the <s>Siddha</s> has foretold the reunion with husband and son, you, unable to bear the separation, should enter the fire!' (Dkc 1,4.4)

children.text: START Dkc 1,4.5:
children.translated_text: START Dkc 1,4.5:

children.text: tanniśamya manoviditajanakabhāvaṃ tamavādiṣam-"tāta, bhavate vijñāpanīyāni bahūni santi /
bhavatu /
children.translated_text: Let it be.

children.text: paścādakhilamākhyātavyam /
children.translated_text: Everything shall be related later.

children.text: adhunā nārīkūjitamanupekṣaṇīyaṃ mayā /
children.translated_text: For now, I must not ignore this woman's cry.

children.text: kṣaṇamātram bhavatā sthīyatām'iti // Dkc_1,4.5 //
children.translated_text: Please wait just a moment.' (Dkc 1,4.5)
Hearing that, and understanding that he was my father — as was known in my mind — I addressed him: 'Father, there is much to be told to you.

children.text: START Dkc 1,4.6:
children.translated_text: START Dkc 1,4.6:

children.text: tadanu so 'haṃ tvarayā kiñcidantaramagamam /
children.translated_text: Thereupon I went quickly a short distance away.

children.text: tatra purato bhayaṅkarajvālākulahutabhugavagāhanasāhasikāṃ mukulitāñjalipuṭāṃ vanitāṃ kāñcidavalokya saṃbhramamanalādapanīya kūjantyā vṛddhayā saha matpiturabhyarṇamabhigamayya sthavirāmavocam-"vṛddhe, bhavatyau kutratye /
children.translated_text: There, seeing before me a woman with folded hands, recklessly about to plunge into a terrifying fire full of blazing flames, I swiftly pulled her back from the fire, and bringing her along with the crying old woman to the vicinity of my father, I addressed the elder: 'Old woman, where are you two from?

children.text: kāntāre nimittena kena duravasthānubhūyate /
children.translated_text: For what reason are you suffering such distress in this wilderness?

children.text: kathyatām' iti // Dkc_1,4.6 //
children.translated_text: Tell me.' (Dkc 1,4.6)

children.text: START Dkc 1,4.7:
children.translated_text: START Dkc 1,4.7:

children.text: sā sagadgadamavādīt-"putra, kālayavanadvīpe kālaguptanāmno vaṇijaḥ kasyacideṣā sutā suvṛttā nāma ratnodbhavena nijakāntenāgacchantī jaladhau magne pravahaṇe nijadhātryā mayā saha phalakamekamavalambya daivayogena kūlamupetāsannaprasavasamayā kasyāñcidaṭavyāmātmajamasūta /
children.translated_text: She spoke with a faltering voice: 'Son, on the island of <s>Kālayavana</s>, this is the daughter of a certain merchant named <s>Kālagupta</s>, named <s>Suvṛttā</s>. While returning with her own husband <s>Ratnodbhava</s>, when the ship sank in the ocean, clinging to a plank along with me, her wet-nurse, she reached the shore by the working of fate. Being near the time of delivery, she gave birth to a son in some forest.

children.text: mama tu mandabhāgyatayā bāle vanamātaṅgena gṛhīte maddvitīyā paribhramantī "ṣoḍaśavarṣānantaraṃ bhartṛputrasaṅgamo bhaviṣyati' iti siddhavākyaviśvāsādekasminpuṇyāśrame tāvantaṃ samayaṃ nītvā śokamapāraṃ soḍhumakṣamā samujjvalite vaiśvānare śarīramāhutīkartumudyuktāsīt' iti // Dkc_1,4.7 //
children.translated_text: But by my ill fortune, when the child was seized by a wild elephant, she, accompanied only by me, wandering about, trusting in the words of a <s>Siddha</s> (perfected sage) that "after sixteen years there will be reunion with husband and son," having passed that length of time in a sacred hermitage, and unable to bear the boundless grief any longer, was about to offer her body as an oblation into the blazing fire.' (Dkc 1,4.7)

children.text: START Dkc 1,4.8:
children.translated_text: START Dkc 1,4.8:

children.text: tadākarṇya nijajananīṃ jñātvā tāmahaṃ daṇḍavatpraṇamya tasyai madudantamakhilamākhyāya dhātrībhāṣaṇaphullavadanaṃ vismayavikasitākṣaṃ janakamadarśayam /
children.translated_text: Hearing that, recognizing her as my own mother, I prostrated before her like a staff, related to her my entire story, and showed her my father whose face had blossomed at the nurse's words and whose eyes were wide with amazement.

children.text: pitarau tau sābhijñānamanyonyaṃ jñātvā muditāntarātmānau vinītaṃ māmānandāśruvarṣeṇābiṣicya gāḍhamāśliṣya śirasyupāghrāya kasyāñcinmahīruhacchāyāyāmupāviśatām // Dkc_1,4.8 //
children.translated_text: Those two parents, recognizing each other with clear understanding, their hearts filled with joy, consecrated the dutiful me with a shower of tears of happiness, embraced me tightly, smelled my head, and sat down in the shade of some tree. (Dkc 1,4.8)

children.text: START Dkc 1,4.9:
children.translated_text: START Dkc 1,4.9:

children.text: `kathaṃ nivasati mahīvallabho rājahaṃsaḥ' iti janakena pṛṣṭo 'haṃ tasya rājyacyutiṃ tvadīyajananaṃ sakalakumārāvāptiṃ tava digvijayārambho bhavataḥ mātaṅgānuyānamasmākaṃ yuṣmadanveṣaṇakāraṇaṃ sakalamabhyadhām /
children.translated_text: When asked by my father, 'How does the lord of the earth, <s>Rājahaṃsa</s>, fare?', I related to him everything: the loss of his kingdom, your birth, the gathering of all the princes, your commencement of the conquest of the directions, your pursuit of elephants, and the reason for our search for you.

children.text: tatastau kasyacidāśrame munerasthāpayam /
children.translated_text: Then I settled those two in the hermitage of some sage.

children.text: tato devasyānveṣaṇaparāyaṇo 'hamakhilakāryanimittaṃ vittaṃ niścitya bhavadanugrahāllabdhasya sādhakasya sāhāyyakaraṇadakṣaṃ śiṣyagaṇaṃ niṣpādya vindhyavanamadhye purātanapattanasthānānyupetya vividhasūcakānāṃ mahīruhāṇāmadhonikṣiptān vasupūrṇān kalaśān siddhāñjanena jñātvā rakṣiṣu paritaḥ sthiteṣu khananasādhanairutpāṭya dīnārānasaṃkhyān rāśīkṛtya tatkālāgatamanatidūre niveśitaṃ vaṇikkaṭakaṃ kañcidabhyetya tatra balino balīvardān goṇīṃśca krītvānyadravyamiṣeṇa vasu tadgoṇīsañcitaṃ tairuhyamānaṃ śanaiḥ kaṭakamanayam // Dkc_1,4.9 //
children.translated_text: Then, devoted to searching for the lord, having secured wealth for all purposes, and having trained a capable group of disciples of a <s>sādhaka</s> (adept) obtained by your grace to assist in his work, I went to ancient town-sites in the <s>Vindhya</s> forest and, discovering by means of magical collyrium the treasure-filled pots buried beneath various indicator-trees, with guards stationed all around, I dug them up with excavation tools, heaped up countless <s>dīnāras</s> (gold coins), and approaching a merchant caravan that had arrived nearby, I purchased strong bullocks and sacks there, and under the pretext of other merchandise, slowly brought the wealth, packed in those sacks and carried by them, to the caravan. (Dkc 1,4.9)

children.text: START Dkc 1,4.10:
children.translated_text: START Dkc 1,4.10:

children.text: tadadhikāriṇā candrapālena kenacidvaṇikputreṇa viracitasauhṛdo 'hamamunaiva sākamujjayinīmupāviśam /
children.translated_text: Having formed a friendship with a certain merchant's son named <s>Candrapāla</s> who was in charge of that [caravan], I settled with him in <s>Ujjayinī</s>.

children.text: yatpitarāvapi tāṃ purīmabhigamayya sakalaguṇanilayena bandhupālanāmnā candrapālajanakena nīyamāno mālavanāthadarśanaṃ vidhāya tadanumatyā gūḍhavasatimakaravam /
children.translated_text: My parents too, having come to that city, being guided by <s>Bandhupāla</s>, <s>Candrapāla</s>'s father who was an abode of all virtues, obtained an audience with the lord of <s>Mālava</s> and, with his permission, I took up a secret residence.

children.text: tataḥ kānanabhūmiṣu bhavantamanveṣṭumudyuktaṃ māṃ paramamitraṃ bandhupālo niśamyāvadat-"sakalaṃ dharaṇitalamapāramanveṣṭumakṣamo bhavānmanoglāniṃ vihāya tūṣṇīṃ tiṣṭhatu /
children.translated_text: Then, when <s>Bandhupāla</s> learned that I, my dearest friend, was setting out to search for you in the forest regions, he said: 'You are unable to search the entire boundless surface of the earth. Give up your mental anguish and remain quiet.

children.text: bhavannāyakālokanakāraṇaṃ śubhaśakunaṃ nirīkṣya kathayiṣyāmi, iti // Dkc_1,4.10 //
children.translated_text: I shall observe auspicious omens and tell you the means of seeing your lord.' (Dkc 1,4.10)

children.text: START Dkc 1,4.11:
children.translated_text: START Dkc 1,4.11:

children.text: tallapitāmṛtāśvāsitahṛdayo 'hamanudinaṃ tadupakaṇṭhavartī kadācidindumukhīṃ navayauvanālīḍhāvayavāṃ nayanacandrikāṃ bālacandrikāṃ nāma taruṇīratnaṃ vaṇiṅmandiralakṣmīṃ mūrtāmivāvalokya tadīyalāvaṇyāvadhūtadhīrabhāvo latāntabāṇabāṇalakṣyatāmayāsiṣam // Dkc_1,4.11 //
children.translated_text: I, my heart consoled by the nectar of his words, being daily in his vicinity, one day beheld a young woman named <s>Bālacandrikā</s>, a jewel among young women, like the embodied beauty of a merchant's mansion, moon-faced, her limbs embraced by fresh youth, a moonbeam for the eyes. Seeing her, my steadfastness was overwhelmed by her loveliness, and I became the target of the arrows of the flower-bowed <s>Kāma</s> (Love). (Dkc 1,4.11)

children.text: START Dkc 1,4.12:
children.translated_text: START Dkc 1,4.12:

children.text: cakitabālakuraṅgalocanā sāpi kusumasāyakasāyakāyamānena kaṭākṣavīkṣaṇena māmasakṛnnirīkṣya mandamārutāndolitā latevākampata /
children.translated_text: She too, with eyes like those of a startled young doe, repeatedly glanced at me with sidelong looks sharpened by the arrows of <s>Kusumāyudha</s> (the Flower-Weaponed, i.e., <s>Kāma</s>), and trembled like a vine swayed by a gentle breeze.

children.text: manasābhimukhaiḥ samākuñcitai rāgalajjāntarālavartibhiḥ sāṅgavartibhirīkṣaṇaviśeṣairnijamanovṛttimakathayat // Dkc_1,4.12 //
children.translated_text: Through special glances directed toward me from her mind — restrained, hovering between passion and modesty, yet expressing the movements of her whole being — she silently conveyed the inclinations of her heart. (Dkc 1,4.12)

children.text: START Dkc 1,4.13:
children.translated_text: START Dkc 1,4.13:

children.text: caturagūḍhaceṣṭābhirasyā mano 'nurāgaṃ samyagjñātvā sukhasaṃgamopāyamacintayam /
children.translated_text: Having fully understood from those artful yet unaffected gestures the love in her heart, I pondered a means for a happy union.

children.text: anyadā bandhupālaḥ śakunairbhavadgatiṃ praikṣiṣyamāṇaḥ puropāntavihāravanaṃ mayā sahopetya kasmiṃścinmahīruhe śakuntavacanāni śṛṇvannatiṣṭhat // Dkc_1,4.13 //
children.translated_text: On another occasion, <s>Bandhupāla</s>, about to divine your whereabouts from bird-omens, went with me to a pleasure garden on the outskirts of the city and stood under a certain tree listening to the words of birds. (Dkc 1,4.13)

children.text: START Dkc 1,4.14:
children.translated_text: START Dkc 1,4.14:

children.text: ahamutkalikāvinodaparāyaṇo vanāntare paribhramansarovaratīre cintākrāntacittāṃ dīnavadanāṃ manmanorathaikabhūmiṃ bālacandrikāṃ vyalokayam // Dkc_1,4.14 //
children.translated_text: I, intent on relieving my longing, while wandering in the interior of the forest, beheld <s>Bālacandrikā</s>, the sole abode of my heart's desire, on the bank of a lake, her mind seized by anxiety, her face sorrowful. (Dkc 1,4.14)

children.text: START Dkc 1,4.15:
children.translated_text: START Dkc 1,4.15:

children.text: tasyāḥ sasaṃbhramapremalajjākautukamanoramaṃ līlāvilokanasukhamanubhavan sudatyā vadanāravinde viṣaṇṇabhāvaṃ madanakadanakhedānubhūtaṃ tannimittaṃ jñāsyaṃllīlayā tadupakaṇṭhamupetyāvocam-"sumukhi, tava mukhāravindasya dainyakāraṇaṃ kathaya' iti // Dkc_1,4.15 //
children.translated_text: Enjoying the delight of her playful glances — charming with their blend of startled love, modesty, and curiosity — and observing the dejection on the lotus of the fair-toothed one's face, the suffering inflicted by the torment of <s>Madana</s> (Love), and wishing to know its cause, I playfully approached her and said: 'O beautiful one, tell me the cause of the dejection of your lotus face.' (Dkc 1,4.15)

children.text: START Dkc 1,4.16:
children.translated_text: START Dkc 1,4.16:

children.text: sā rahasyasaṃjātaviśrambhatayā vihāya lajjābhaye śanairabhāṣata-"saumya, mānasāro mālavādhīśvaro vārdhakyasya prabalatayā nijanandanaṃ darpasāramujjayinyāmabhyaṣiñcat /
children.translated_text: She, having gained confidence from the intimacy born in private, casting aside both modesty and fear, spoke softly: 'Friend, <s>Mānasāra</s>, the lord of <s>Mālava</s>, due to the burden of old age, anointed his own son <s>Darpasāra</s> as king in <s>Ujjayinī</s>.

children.text: sa kumāraḥ saptasāgaraparyantaṃ mahīmaṇḍalaṃ pālayiṣyannijapaitṛṣvasreyā uddaṇḍakarmāṇau caṇḍavarmadāruvarmāṇau dharaṇībharaṇe niyujya tapaścaraṇāya rājarājagirimabhyagāt // Dkc_1,4.16 //
children.translated_text: That prince, while governing the circle of the earth extending to the seven oceans, appointed his two paternal cousins, <s>Caṇḍavarman</s> and <s>Dāruvarman</s>, terrible in their deeds, to bear the burden of the earth, and himself departed to <s>Rājarājagiri</s> (King of Kings Mountain) for the practice of austerities.' (Dkc 1,4.16)

children.text: START Dkc 1,4.17:
children.translated_text: START Dkc 1,4.17:

children.text:
rājyaṃ sarvamasapatnaṃ śāsati caṇḍavarmaṇi dāruvarmā mātulāgrajanmanoḥ śāsanamatikramya pāradāryaparadravyāpaharaṇādiduṣkarma kurvāṇo manmathasamānasya bhavato lāvaṇyāttacittāṃ māmekadā vilokya kanyādūṣaṇadoṣaṃ dūrīkṛtya balātkāreṇa rantumudyuṅkte /
taccintayā dainyamagaccham' iti// Dkc_1,4.17 //
children.translated_text: While <s>Caṇḍavarman</s> ruled the entire kingdom without rivals, <s>Dāruvarman</s>, transgressing the commands of his maternal uncle and elder brother, engaging in wicked deeds such as adultery and stealing others' property, one day, seeing me whose heart was captivated by the beauty of you who are equal to <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love), disregarding the sin of defiling a maiden, attempted to enjoy me by force. In anxiety over that, I fell into wretchedness.' (Dkc 1,4.17)

children.text: START Dkc 1,4.18:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,4.18]

children.text: tasyā manogatam, rāgodrekaṃ manmanorathasiddhyantarāyaṃ ca niśamya vāṣpapūrṇalocanāṃ tāmāśvāsya dāruvarmaṇo maraṇopāyaṃ ca vicārya ballabhāmavocam "taruṇi, bhavadabhilāṣiṇaṃ duṣṭahṛdayamenaṃ nihantuṃ mṛdurupāyaḥ kaścin mayā cintyate /
children.translated_text: Having heard her innermost thoughts, the excess of her passion, and the obstacle to the fulfillment of my own desire, I consoled her whose eyes were filled with tears, deliberated upon a means to kill <s>Dāruvarman</s>, and said to my beloved: 'O young woman, some gentle stratagem is being devised by me to slay this evil-hearted one who desires you.

children.text: yakṣaḥ kaścidadhiṣṭhāya bālacandrikāṃ nivasati /
children.translated_text: A certain <s>Yakṣa</s> inhabits <s>Bālacandrikā</s> [as his abode].

children.text: tadākārasaṃpadāśāśṛṅkhalitahṛdayo yaḥ saṃbandhayogyaḥ sāhasiko ratimandire taṃ yakṣaṃ nirjitya tayā ekasakhīsametayā mṛgākṣyā saṃlāpāmṛtasukhamanubhūya kuśalī nirgamiṣyati, tena cakravākasaṃśayākārapayodharā vivāhanīyeti siddhenaikenāvādīti purajanasya purato bhavadīyaiḥ satyavākyairjanairasakṛt kathanīyam /
children.translated_text: "One whose heart is fettered by the chain of hope for the beauty of her form, who is worthy of union [with her], a daring man — having conquered that <s>Yakṣa</s> in the pleasure-house, having enjoyed the nectar-bliss of conversation with that doe-eyed woman accompanied by one female companion, he shall emerge safely" — thus a certain <s>Siddha</s> (perfected one) has declared. This must be repeatedly proclaimed before the townspeople by your trustworthy speakers.

children.text: tadanu dāruvarmā vākyānītthaṃvidhāni śrāvaṃśrāvaṃ tūṣṇīṃ yadi bhiyā sthāsyati tarhi varam, yadi vā daurjanyena tvayā saṃgamaṅgīkariṣyati, tadā sa bhavadīyairitthaṃ vācyaḥ // Dkc_1,4.18 //
children.translated_text: Then, if <s>Dāruvarman</s>, hearing such words again and again, will remain silent out of fear — that would be best; but if through wickedness he agrees to the union with you, then he should be addressed by your people thus:' (Dkc 1,4.18)

children.text: START Dkc 1,4.19:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,4.19]

children.text:
`saumya, darpasāravasudhādhipāmātyasya bhavato 'smannivāse sāhasakaraṇamanucitam /
paurajanasākṣikabhavanmandiramānītayā anayā toyajākṣyā saha krīḍannāyuṣmān yadi bhaviṣyati tadā pariṇīya taruṇīṃ manorathān nirviśa' iti /
so 'pyetadaṅgīkariṣyati /
tvaṃ sakhīveṣadhāriṇā mayā saha tasya mandiraṃ gaccha /
ahamekāntaniketane muṣṭijānupādāghātaistaṃ rabhasānnihatya punarapi vayasyāmiṣeṇa bhavatīmanuniḥśaṅkaṃ nirgamiṣyāmi /
children.translated_text: I, in a secluded corner of the house, shall violently strike him down with blows of fist, knee, and foot, and then again, using the pretext of your friend, I shall depart without suspicion with you.

children.text: tadenamupāyamaṅgīkṛtya vigatasādhvasalajjā bhavajjanakajananīsahodarāṇāṃ purata āvayoḥ premātiśayamākhyāya sarvathāsmatpariṇayakaraṇe tānanunayeḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, having accepted this stratagem, casting off fear and shame, declare the excess of our love before your father, mother, and siblings, and persuade them by all means to arrange our marriage.

children.text: te 'pi vaṃśasaṃpallāvaṇyāḍhyāya yūne mahyaṃ tvāṃ dāsyantyeva /
children.translated_text: They too will certainly give you to me, a youth endowed with noble lineage and beauty.

children.text: dāruvarmaṇo māraṇopāyaṃ tebhyaḥ kathayitvā teṣāmuttaramākhyeyaṃ mahyam' iti // Dkc_1,4.19 //
children.translated_text: Having told them the plan for killing <s>Dāruvarman</s>, you should then convey their response to me.' (Dkc 1,4.19)

'Good sir, it is unbecoming for you, a minister of the great King <s>Darpasāra</s>, to commit acts of violence in our dwelling. If you will sport with this lotus-eyed maiden who has been brought to your pleasure-house with the townspeople as witnesses, then marry the young woman and fulfill your desires.' He too will agree to this. You, go to his pleasure-house with me, who shall be disguised as a female companion.

children.text: START Dkc 1,4.20:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,4.20]

children.text:
sāpi kiñcidutphullasarasijānanā māmabravīt--"subhaga, krūrakarmāṇaṃ dāruvarmāṇaṃ bhavāneva hantumarhati /
tasmin hate sarvathā yuṣmanmanorathaḥ phaliṣyati /
evaṃ kriyatām /
children.translated_text: Let it be done thus.

children.text: bhavaduktaṃ sarvamahamapi tathā kariṣye' iti māmasakṛdvivṛttavadanā vilokayantī mandaṃ mandamagāramagāt /
children.translated_text: I shall carry out everything as you have said' — and gazing at me repeatedly with her face turned back, she slowly departed from the house.

children.text: ahamapi bandhupālamupetya śakunajñāttasmāt triṃśaddivasānantarameva bhavatsaṅgaḥ saṃbhaviṣyati ityaśṛṇavam /
children.translated_text: I too, approaching <s>Bandhupāla</s>, heard from that bird-augur that the union with you would come about after just thirty days.

children.text: tadanu madanugamyamāno bandhupālo nijāvāsaṃ praviśya māmapi nilayāya visasarja // Dkc_1,4.20 //
children.translated_text: Then <s>Bandhupāla</s>, accompanied by me, entered his own dwelling and assigned me quarters as well. (Dkc 1,4.20)

She too, her lotus-face somewhat blooming, said to me: 'O handsome one, you alone are able to slay the cruel <s>Dāruvarman</s>. Once he is killed, your desire will certainly be fulfilled in every way.

children.text: START Dkc 1,4.21:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,4.21]

children.text: manmāyopāyavāgurāpāśalagnena dāruvarmaṇā ratimandire rantuṃ samāhūtā bālacandrikā taṃ gamiṣyantīdūtikāṃ mannikaṭamabhipreṣitavatī /
children.translated_text: <s>Bālacandrikā</s>, summoned by <s>Dāruvarman</s> — who had been ensnared in the trap-net of my deceptive stratagem — to sport in the pleasure-house, being about to go to him, sent a messenger-woman to my side.

children.text: ahamapi maṇinūpuramekhalākaṅkaṇakaṭakataṭaṅkahārakṣaumakajjalaṃ vanitāyogyaṃ maṇḍanajātaṃ nipuṇatayā tattatsthāneṣu nikṣipya samyagaṅgīkṛtamanojñaveśo vallabhayā tayā saha tadāgāradvāropāntamagaccham // Dkc_1,4.21 //
children.translated_text: I too, placing in their proper places with great skill the ornamental items appropriate for a woman — gem-anklets, girdle, bracelets, armlets, pendant-earrings, necklace, silk garment, and collyrium — having perfectly assumed a charming feminine attire, went with my beloved to the entrance of that house. (Dkc 1,4.21)

children.text: START Dkc 1,4.22:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,4.22]

children.text: dvāḥsthakathitāsmadāgamanena sādaraṃ vihitābhyudgatinā tena dvāropāntanivāritāśeṣaparivāreṇa madanvitā bālacandrikā saṅketāgāramanīyata /
children.translated_text: Informed of our arrival by the doorkeeper, <s>Bālacandrikā</s>, accompanied by me, was led into the pleasure-chamber by him who had respectfully risen to greet us and had dismissed all attendants from the entrance.

children.text: nagaravyākulāṃ yakṣakathāṃ parīkṣamāṇo nāgarikajano 'pi kutūhalena dāruvarmaṇaḥ pratīhārabhūmimagamat // Dkc_1,4.22 //
children.translated_text: The townspeople too, examining the rumor about the <s>Yakṣa</s> that had spread through the city, came out of curiosity to <s>Dāruvarman</s>'s antechamber. (Dkc 1,4.22)

children.text: START Dkc 1,4.23:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,4.23]

children.text: vivekaśūnyamatirasau rāgātirekeṇa ratnakhacitahemaparyaṅke haṃsatūlagarbhaśayanamānīya taruṇīṃ, tasyai mahyaṃ tamisrāsamyaganavalokitapuṃbhāvāya manoramastrīveśāya ca cāmīkaramaṇimaṇḍanāni sūkṣmāṇi citravastrāṇi kastūrikāmilitaṃ haricandanaṃ karpūrasahitaṃ tāmbūlaṃ surabhīṇi kusumānītyādivastujātaṃ samarpya muhūrtadvayamātraṃ hāsavacanaiḥ saṃlapannatiṣṭhat // Dkc_1,4.23 //
children.translated_text: That one, devoid of prudence, in his excess of passion, having placed the young woman upon a couch of jewel-encrusted gold with a mattress stuffed with swan's down, presented to her — and to me, whose masculinity had not been properly discerned in the darkness and whose charming feminine disguise [was convincing] — golden ornaments set with gems, fine colorful garments, sandalwood mixed with musk, betel with camphor, fragrant flowers, and such articles, and stood conversing with jesting words for just two <s>muhūrtas</s> (about an hour and a half). (Dkc 1,4.23)

children.text: START Dkc 1,4.24:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,4.24]

children.text: tato rāgāndhatayā sumukhīkucagrahaṇe matiṃ vyadhatta /
roṣāruṇito 'hamenaṃ paryaṅkatalānniḥśaṅko nipātya muṣṭijānupādaghātaiḥ prāharam /
children.translated_text: Reddened with rage, I unhesitatingly threw him down from the couch and struck him with blows of fist, knee, and foot.

children.text: niyuddharabhasavikalālaṅkāraṃ pūrvavanmelayitvā bhayakampitāṃ natāṅgīmupalālayanmandirāṅgaṇamupetaḥ sādhvasakampita ivoccairakūjamaham--"hā, bālacandrikādhiṣṭhitena ghorākāreṇa yakṣeṇa dāruvarmā nihanyate /
children.translated_text: Having rearranged as before the ornaments that had become disarrayed in the violence of the struggle, caressing the trembling and cowering young woman, I reached the courtyard of the pleasure-house and cried out loudly, as if trembling with fear: 'Alas! <s>Dāruvarman</s> is being slain by a fierce-looking <s>Yakṣa</s> who has possessed <s>Bālacandrikā</s>!

children.text: sahasā samāgacchata /
children.translated_text: Come quickly!

children.text: paśyatemam iti // Dkc_1,4.24 //
children.translated_text: Look at this!' (Dkc 1,4.24)
Then, blinded by passion, he set his mind upon seizing the beautiful woman's breasts.

children.text: START Dkc 1,4.25:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,4.25]

children.text: tadākarṇya militā janā samudyadvāṣpā hāhānidānena diśo badhirayantaḥ bālacandrikāmadhiṣṭhitaṃ yakṣaṃ balavantaṃ śṛṇvannapi dāruvarmā madāndhastāmevāyācata /
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the assembled people, their eyes brimming with tears, deafening the quarters with cries of 'Alas, alas!' — even though hearing that a powerful <s>Yakṣa</s> had possessed <s>Bālacandrikā</s>, <s>Dāruvarman</s>, blinded by lust, still desired her.

children.text: tadasau svakīyena karmaṇā nihataḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus he was slain by his own [evil] deed.

children.text: "kiṃ tasya vilāpena' iti mitho lapantaḥ prāviśan /
children.translated_text: 'What is the use of lamenting for him?' — thus speaking among themselves, they entered.

children.text: kolāhale tasmiṃścalalocanayā saha naipuṇyena sahasā nirgato nijānuvāsamagām // Dkc_1,4.25 //
children.translated_text: In that commotion, having deftly and swiftly slipped out with the darting-eyed one, I went to my own lodging. (Dkc 1,4.25)

children.text: START Dkc 1,4.26:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,4.26]

children.text: tato gateṣu katipayadineṣu paurajanasamakṣaṃ siddhādeśaprakāreṇa vivāhya tāmindumukhīṃ pūrvasaṃkalpitān surataviśeṣān yatheṣṭamanvabhūvam /
children.translated_text: Then, after some days had passed, having married that moon-faced maiden before the townspeople in the manner prescribed by the <s>Siddha</s>'s prediction, I enjoyed at will the special pleasures of love that I had previously imagined.

children.text: bandhupālaśakunanirdiṣṭe divase 'sminnirgatya purādbahirvartamāno netrotsavakāri bhavadavalokanasukhamanubhavāmi iti // Dkc_1,4.26 //
children.translated_text: On the day indicated by <s>Bandhupāla</s>'s bird-augury, having gone out of the city and being nearby, I am now experiencing the delight of beholding your eye-festival-causing [presence]. (Dkc 1,4.26)

children.text: START Dkc 1,4.27:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,4.27]

children.text: evaṃ mitravṛttāntaṃ niśamyāmlānamānaso rājavāhanaḥ svasya ca somadattasya ca vṛttāntamasmai nivedya somadattaṃ "mahākāleśvarārādhanānantaraṃ bhavadvallabhāṃ saparivārāṃ nijakaṭakaṃ prāpayyāgaccha' iti niyujya puṣpodbhavena sevyamāno bhūsvargāyamānamavantikāpuraṃ viveśa /
children.translated_text: Thus, having heard the account of his friend and with a downcast mind, <s>Rājavāhana</s>, having related to him the account of himself and <s>Somadatta</s>, instructed <s>Somadatta</s>: 'After worshipping Lord <s>Mahākāleśvara</s>, bring your beloved with her retinue to my camp and come [back].' Attended by <s>Puṣpodbhava</s>, he entered the city of <s>Avantikā</s> (Ujjain), which rivaled heaven on earth.

children.text: tatra "ayaṃ mama svāmikumāraḥ' iti bandhupālādaye bandhujanāya kathayitvā tena rājavāhanāya bahuvidhāṃ saparyāṃ kārayan sakalakalākuśalo mahīsuravara iti puri prakaṭayan puṣpodbhavo 'muṣyarājño majjanabhojanādikamanudinaṃ svamandire kārayāmāsa // Dkc_1,4.27 //
children.translated_text: There, <s>Puṣpodbhava</s>, having told the kinfolk led by <s>Bandhupāla</s> that 'This is my lord the prince,' causing them to render manifold homage to <s>Rājavāhana</s>, making known in the city [his own fame] as 'one accomplished in all arts, foremost among the learned,' had the bathing, dining, and other daily [services] of that prince performed in his own mansion. (Dkc 1,4.27)

children.text: iti śrīdaṇḍinaḥ kṛtau daśakumāracarite puṣpodbhavacaritaṃ nāma caturtha ucchvāsaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth <s>ucchvāsa</s> (chapter), named 'The Adventures of <s>Puṣpodbhava</s>,' in the <s>Daśakumāracarita</s> composed by the illustrious <s>Daṇḍin</s>.

children.text: pañcamocchvāsaḥ
children.translated_text: The Fifth <s>Ucchvāsa</s> (Chapter).

children.text: START Dkc 1,5.1:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,5.1]

children.text: atha mīnaketanasenānāyakena malayagirimahīruhanirantarāvāsibhujaṅgamabhuktāvaśiṣṭeneva sūkṣmatareṇa dhṛtaharicandanaparimalabhareṇeva mandagatinā dakṣiṇānilena viyogihṛdayasthaṃ manmathānalamujjvalayan, sahakārakisalayamakarandāsvādanaraktakaṇṭhānāṃ madhukarakalakaṇṭhānāṃ kākalīkalakalena dikcakraṃ vācālayan māninīmānasotkalikāmupanayan mākandasinduvāraraktāśokakiṃśukatilakeṣu kalikāmupapādayan, madanamahotsavāya rasikamanāṃsi samullāsayan, vasantasamayaḥ samājagāma // Dkc_1,5.1 //
children.translated_text: Then, with a breeze from the south that was the commander of the army of <s>Mīnaketana</s> (<s>Kāmadeva</s>, the god of love), gentle in motion as if carrying a cargo of fragrance of sandalwood wood from the <s>Malaya</s> mountain — [a breeze] as subtle as the remnant left by serpents dwelling ceaselessly among the great trees of the <s>Malaya</s> mountain — fanning the fire of <s>Manmatha</s> (love) stationed in the hearts of those separated [from their beloveds]; making the quarters resound with the melodious warbling of intoxicated bees whose throats were reddened by tasting the nectar of mango blossoms; arousing the surging emotions in the minds of proud women; producing buds on the <s>makanda</s> (mango), <s>sinduvāra</s>, <s>raktāśoka</s>, <s>kiṃśuka</s>, and <s>tilaka</s> trees; gladdening the hearts of connoisseurs for the great festival of <s>Madana</s> (love) — the spring season arrived. (Dkc 1,5.1)

children.text: START Dkc 1,5.2:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,5.2]

children.text: tasminnatiramaṇīye kāle 'vantisundarī nāma mānasāranandinī priyavayasyayā bālacandrikayā saha nagaropāntaramyodyāne vihārotkaṇṭhayā paurasundarīsamavāyasamanvitā kasyaciccūtapotakasya chāyāśītale saikatatale gandhakusumaharidrākṣatacīnāmbarādinānāvidhena parimaladravyanikareṇa manobhavamarcayantī reme // Dkc_1,5.2 //
children.translated_text: In that most delightful season, a woman named <s>Avantisundarī</s>, daughter of <s>Mānasāra</s>, accompanied by her dear friend <s>Bālacandrikā</s>, eager for amusement in a charming garden on the outskirts of the city, attended by an assembly of beautiful women of the city, was enjoying herself at the cool, sandy bank in the shade of a certain young mango tree, worshipping <s>Manobhava</s> (the god of love) with a multitude of fragrant substances of various kinds — incense, flowers, turmeric, unbroken rice, fine Chinese silk, and so on. (Dkc 1,5.2)

children.text: START Dkc 1,5.3:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,5.3]

children.text: tatra ratipratikṛtimavantisundarīṃ draṣṭukāmaḥ kāma iva vasantasahāyaḥ puṣpodbhavasamanvito rājavāhanastadupavanaṃ praviśya tatra tatra malayamārutāndolitaśākhānirantarasamudbhinnakisalayakusumaphalasamullasiteṣu rasālataruṣu kokilakīrālikulamadhukarāṇāmālāpāñśrāvaṃ śrāvaṃ kiñcidvikasadindīvarakahlārakairavarājīvarājīkelilola-kalahaṃsa-sārasa-kāraṇḍava-cakravāka-cakravāla-kalaravavyākulavimalaśītalasal ilalalitāni sarāṃsi darśandarśamamandalīlayā lalanāsamīpamavāpa // Dkc_1,5.3 //
children.translated_text: There, desiring to see <s>Avantisundarī</s>, who was like an image of <s>Rati</s>, <s>Rājavāhana</s>, accompanied by <s>Puṣpodbhava</s> like <s>Kāma</s> accompanied by <s>Vasanta</s> (Spring), entered that pleasure garden, and there, hearing again and again the calls of <s>kokila</s>s (cuckoos), parrots, bee-swarms, and <s>madhukaras</s> (honey-bees) in the mango trees that were resplendent with shoots, blossoms, and fruits ceaselessly bursting forth from branches swaying in the <s>Malaya</s> breeze, beholding the lakes — beautiful with cool, clear, playful waters, turbulent with the clamor of flocks of <s>kalahaṃsa</s>s (swans), <s>sārasa</s>s (cranes), <s>kāraṇḍava</s>s (ducks), and <s>cakravāka</s>s (ruddy geese) sporting playfully among rows of lotuses where <s>indīvara</s>s (blue lotuses) and <s>kahlāra</s>s (white lotuses) were slightly blooming — he reached the vicinity of the lady without haste. [Dkc 1,5.3]

children.text: START Dkc 1,5.4:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,5.4]

children.text: bālacandrikayā 'niḥśaṅkamita āgamyatām' iti hastasaṃjñayā samāhūto nijatejonirjitapuruhūto rājavāhanaḥ kṛśodaryā avantisundaryā antikaṃ samājagāma // Dkc_1,5.4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rājavāhana</s>, whose splendor surpassed that of <s>Puruhūta</s> (<s>Indra</s>), summoned by <s>Bālacandrikā</s> with a hand-gesture saying 'Come here without fear,' approached the presence of the slender-waisted <s>Avantisundarī</s>. [Dkc 1,5.4]

children.text: START Dkc 1,5.5:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,5.5]

children.text: yā vasantasahāyena samutsukatayā rate kelīśālabhañjikāvidhitsayā kañcana nārīviśeṣaṃ viracyātmanaḥ krīḍākāsāraśāradāravindasaundaryeṇa pādadvayam, udyānavanadīrghikāmattamarālikāgamanarītyā līlālasagativilāsam, tūṇīralāvaṇyena jaṅghe, līlāmandiradvārakadalīlālityena manojñamūruyugam, jaitrarathacāturyeṇa ghanaṃ jaghanam kiñcidvikasallīlāvataṃsakahlārakorakakoṭarānuvṛttyā gaṅgāvartasanābhiṃ nābhim, saudhārohaṇaparipāṭyā valitrayam, maurvīmadhukarapaṅktinīlimalīlayā romāvalim pūrṇasuvarṇakalaśaśobhayā kucadvandvam,(latāmaṇḍapasaukumāryeṇa bāhū), jayaśaṅkhābhikhyayā kaṇṭham, kamanīyakarṇapūrasahakārapallavarāgeṇa pratibimbīkṛtabimbaṃ radanacchadanaṃ bāṇāyamānapuṣpalāvaṇyena śuci smitam, agradūtikākalakaṇṭhikākalālāpamādhuryeṇa vacanajātam, sakalasainikanāyakamalayamārutasaurabhyeṇa niḥśvāsapavanam jayadhvajamīnadarpeṇa locanayugalam, cāpayaṣṭiśriyā bhrūlate, prathamasuhṛdasudhākarasyāpanītakalaṅkayā kāntyā vadanam, (līlāmayūrabarhabhaṅgyā keśapāśaṃ) ca vidhāya samastamakarandakastūrikāsammitena malayajarasena prakṣālya karpūraparāgeṇa sammṛjya nirmiteva rarāja // Dkc_1,5.5 //
children.translated_text: She — whom <s>Rati</s> (the goddess of love), with <s>Vasanta</s> (Spring) as her helper, eagerly fashioning a certain extraordinary woman as if creating a <s>śālabhañjikā</s> (ornamental statue) for her pleasure-hall, appeared to have crafted and then bathed in <s>malayaja</s> (sandalwood) paste equal in fragrance to all combined <s>makaranda</s> (flower nectar) and <s>kastūrikā</s> (musk), and polished with <s>karpūra</s> (camphor) dust, so that she shone as if artfully made — her two feet with the beauty of autumn lotuses in a pleasure-pond, her gait with the graceful languid movement of an intoxicated <s>marālī</s> (female swan) walking along a long garden canal, her shanks with the elegance of quivers, her lovely pair of thighs with the charm of plantain trees at the doorway of a pleasure-pavilion, her dense hips with the artistry of a triumphal chariot, her navel deep like a whirlpool of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> following the hollow of a slightly blooming <s>kahlāra</s> (lotus) bud worn as a playful ear-ornament, her three folds of skin at the waist with the pattern of ascending a palace stairway, her line of hair with the dark beauty of a row of bees on a bowstring, her pair of breasts with the splendor of full golden pitchers, her arms with the delicacy of a bower of creepers, her neck with the appearance of a conch of victory, her lips reflecting <s>bimba</s> fruits with the redness of a mango shoot worn as a lovely ear-ornament, her pure smile with the beauty of an arrow-length flower, her speech with the sweetness of the melodious prattle of a <s>kalakaṇṭhikā</s> (Indian cuckoo) serving as a forerunner, her breath-wind with the fragrance of the <s>Malaya</s> breeze that is the commander of all soldiers, her pair of eyes with the pride of the fish on a victory-banner, her eyebrow-creepers with the beauty of a bow-shaft, her face with the radiance of the moon — the first friend — whose blemish had been removed, and her mass of hair with the curve of a playful peacock's tail-feathers — she shone resplendent. [Dkc 1,5.5]

children.text: START Dkc 1,5.6:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,5.6]

children.text: sā mūrtimatīva lakṣmīrmālaveśakanyakā svenaivārādhyamānaṃ saṅkalpitavarapradānāyāvirbhūtaṃ mūrtimantaṃ manmathamiva tamālokya mandamārutāndolitā lateva madanāveśavatī cakampe /
children.translated_text: That princess of <s>Mālava</s>, like <s>Lakṣmī</s> incarnate, upon beholding him — who appeared as if <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love) had manifested in bodily form to grant the boon she had wished for, and whom she herself was worshipping — trembled like a creeper swayed by a gentle breeze, overcome by the passion of <s>Madana</s> (love).

children.text: tadanu krīḍāviśrambhānnivṛttā lajjayā kāni kānyapi bhāvāntarāṇi vyadhatta // Dkc_1,5.6 //
children.translated_text: Then, withdrawing from the abandon of playfulness out of modesty, she assumed various other expressions and attitudes. [Dkc 1,5.6]

children.text: START Dkc 1,5.7:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,5.7]

children.text: lalanājanaṃ sṛjatā vidhātrā nūnameṣā ghuṇākṣaranyāyena nirmitā /
children.translated_text: Surely, when <s>Vidhātṛ</s> (the Creator) was creating womankind, this one was fashioned by the principle of <s>ghuṇākṣara</s> (the woodworm's accidental letter) — that is, by a lucky accident.

children.text: no cedabjabhūrevaṃvidho nirmāṇanipuṇo yadi syāttarhi tatsamānalāvaṇyāmanyāṃ taruṇīṃ kiṃ na karoti' iti savismayānurāgaṃ vilokayatastasya samakṣaṃ sthātuṃ lajjitā satī kiñcitsakhījanāntaritagātrā tannayananābhimukhaiḥ kiñcidākuñcitabhrūlatairapāṅgavīkṣitairātmanaḥkuraṅgasyānāyamānalāvaṇyaṃ rājavāhanaṃ vilokayantyatiṣṭhat // Dkc_1,5.7 //
children.translated_text: Otherwise, if the lotus-born <s>Brahmā</s> were truly so skilled in creation, why would he not make another young woman of equal beauty?' — as he gazed at her thus with wonder and love, she, embarrassed to stand before his eyes, partly concealing her body behind her companions, stood gazing at <s>Rājavāhana</s> — whose beauty surpassed that of her own pet deer — with sidelong glances from beneath slightly arched eyebrow-creepers directed toward his eyes. [Dkc 1,5.7]

children.text: START Dkc 1,5.8:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,5.8]

children.text: so 'pi tasyāstadotpāditabhāvarasānāṃ sāmagryā labdhabalasyeva viṣamaśarasya śaravyāyamāṇamānaso babhūva // Dkc_1,5.8 //
children.translated_text: He too became a target for the mind of <s>Viṣamaśara</s> (the god of love, 'he of uneven arrows'), who seemed to have gained strength from the full arsenal of amorous sentiments she had aroused. [Dkc 1,5.8]

children.text: START Dkc 1,5.9:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,5.9]

children.text:
sā manasītthamacintayat-"ananyasādhāraṇasaundaryeṇānena kasyāṃ puri bhāgyavatīnāṃ taruṇīnāṃ locanotsavaḥ kriyate /
putraratnenāmunā purandhrīṇāṃ putravatīnāṃ sīmantinīnāṃ kā nāma sīmantamauktikīkriyate /
kāsya devī /
kimatrāgamanakāraṇamasya /
children.translated_text: What is the reason for his coming here?

children.text: manmatho māmapahasitanijalāvaṇyamenaṃ vilokayantīmasūyayevātimātraṃ mathnannijanāma sānvayaṃ karoti /
children.translated_text: <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love), as if out of jealousy seeing me gaze at this one whose beauty puts his own to shame, churns me excessively, thus making his name ('the Churner') true to its etymology.

children.text: kiṃ karomi /
children.translated_text: What shall I do?

children.text: kathamayaṃ jñātavya' iti // Dkc_1,5.9 //
children.translated_text: How can this man be identified?' [Dkc 1,5.9]

She thought thus in her mind: 'In which city does this one, of beauty shared with no other, create a festival for the eyes of fortunate young women? Among women blessed with sons, which <s>sīmantinī</s> (married woman) is made the foremost by this jewel of a son? Who is his queen?

children.text: START Dkc 1,5.10:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,5.10]

children.text: tato bālacandrikā tayorantaraṅgavṛttiṃ bhāvavivekairjñātvā kāntāsamājasannidhau rājanandanodantasya samyagākhyānamanucitamiti lokasādhāraṇairvākyairabhāṣata-"bhartṛdārike, ayaṃ sakalakalāpravīṇo devatāsānnidhyakaraṇa āhavanipuṇo bhūsurakumāro maṇimantrauṣadhijñaḥ paricaryārhe bhavatyā pūjyatām' iti // Dkc_1,5.10 //
children.translated_text: Then <s>Bālacandrikā</s>, having discerned through her perceptive reading of emotions the inner feelings of those two, considering that a full account of the prince's story would be improper in the presence of a gathering of ladies, spoke in words of general applicability: 'Noble princess, this young <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, proficient in all arts, skilled in performing rituals that invoke the presence of deities, knowledgeable in gems, <s>mantras</s> (sacred formulas), and herbs, should be honored by you who are worthy of such service.' [Dkc 1,5.10]

children.text: START Dkc 1,5.11:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,5.11]

children.text: tadākarṇya nijamanorathamanuvadantyā bālacandrikayā santuṣṭāntaraṅgā taraṅgāvalī mandānileneva saṅkalpajenākulīkṛtā rājakanyā jitamāraṃ kumāraṃ samucitāsīnaṃ vidhāya sakhīhastena śastena gandhakusumākṣataghanasāratāmbūlādinānājātivastunicayena pūjāṃ tasmai kārayāmāsa /
rājavāhano 'pyevamacintayat-"nūnameṣā pūrvajanmani me jāyā yajñavatī /
children.translated_text: <s>Rājavāhana</s> too thought thus: 'Surely this one was my wife <s>Yajñavatī</s> in a former birth.

children.text: no cedetasyāmevaṃvidho 'nurāgo manmanasi na jāyeta /
children.translated_text: Otherwise, such love for her would not arise in my heart.

children.text: śāpāvasānasamaye taponidhidattaṃ jātismaratvamāvayoḥ samānameva /
children.translated_text: At the end of the curse's duration, the memory of past lives granted by the treasure-house of <s>tapas</s> (ascetic power) is the same for both of us.

children.text: tathāpi kālajanitaviśeṣasūcakavākyairasyā jñānamutpādayiṣyāmi'iti // Dkc_1,5.11 //
children.translated_text: Even so, I shall awaken her knowledge through words that hint at the distinctive marks produced by time.' [Dkc 1,5.11]

Hearing that, the royal maiden — inwardly delighted by <s>Bālacandrikā</s> who was echoing her own heart's desire, agitated by the passion born of longing like a series of waves stirred by a gentle wind — had <s>Kumāra</s> (the prince), who had conquered <s>Māra</s> (the god of love in beauty), seated in a fitting place, and through the hand of her companion had worship offered to him with a collection of various substances: sandalwood paste, flowers, <s>akṣata</s> (unbroken rice grains), dense <s>sāra</s> (essence/incense), <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel), and other offerings of various kinds.

children.text: START Dkc 1,5.12:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,5.12]

children.text: tasminneva samaye ko 'pi manoramo rājahaṃsaḥ kelīvidhitsayā tadupakaṇṭhamagamat /
children.translated_text: At that very moment, a certain beautiful royal swan came near that place, desiring to sport.

children.text: samutsukayā rājakanyayā marālagrahaṇe niyuktāṃ bālacandrikāmavalokya samucito vākyāvasara iti sambhāṣaṇanipuṇo rājavāhanaḥ salīlamalapat--"sakhi, purā śāmbo nāma kaścinmahīvallabho manovallabhayā saha vihāravāñchayā kamalākaramavāpya tatra kokanadakadambasamīpe nidrādhīnamānasaṃ rājahaṃsaṃ śanairgṛhītvā bisaguṇena tasya caraṇayugalaṃ nigaḍayitvā kāntāmukhaṃ sānurāgaṃ vilokayanmandasmitavikasitaikakapolamaṇḍalastāmabhāṣata-"indumukhi, mayā baddho marālaḥ śānto munivadāste /
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Bālacandrikā</s> engaged by the eager princess in catching the swan, <s>Rājavāhana</s>, skilled in conversation, thinking 'this is the right moment for speech,' spoke playfully: 'Friend, once upon a time a certain lord of the earth named <s>Śāmba</s>, having come to a lotus pond with his beloved desiring to sport, there gently seized a royal swan that had fallen asleep near a cluster of red lotuses, bound its pair of feet with a lotus-stalk fiber, and gazing lovingly at the face of his beloved with a gentle smile blooming on one cheek, said to her: "O moon-faced one, the swan I have bound sits peacefully like a <s>muni</s> (sage).

children.text: svecchayānena gamyatām'iti // Dkc_1,5.12 //
children.translated_text: Let it go at its own will."' [Dkc 1,5.12]

children.text: START Dkc 1,5.13:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,5.13]

children.text: so 'pi rājahaṃsaḥ śāmbamaśapat-"mahīpāla, yadasminnambujakhaṇḍe 'nuṣṭhānaparāyaṇatayā paramānandena tiṣṭhantaṃ naiṣṭhikaṃ māmakāraṇaṃ rājyagarveṇāvamānitavānasi tadetatpāpmanā ramaṇīvirahasantāpamanubhava' iti /
children.translated_text: That royal swan then cursed <s>Śāmba</s>: 'O king, because you, out of royal arrogance, have without cause insulted me — a celibate devotee dwelling in supreme bliss, devoted to my practice in this lotus grove — therefore, by this sin, suffer the burning anguish of separation from your beloved!'

children.text: viṣaṇṇavadanaḥ śāmbo jīviteśvarīvirahasahiṣṇurbhūmau daṇḍavatpraṇamya savinayamabhāṣata-"mahābhāga, yadajñānenākaravam tatkṣamasva' iti /
children.translated_text: With a crestfallen face, <s>Śāmba</s>, unable to bear separation from the lady of his life, prostrated himself on the ground like a staff and spoke humbly: 'Great one, forgive what I did out of ignorance.'

children.text: sa tāpasaḥ karuṇākṛṣṭacetāstamavadat-"rājan !iha janmani bhavataḥ śāpaphalābhāvo bhavatu /
children.translated_text: That ascetic, his heart moved by compassion, said to him: 'O king! Let the fruit of the curse not take effect in this birth.

children.text: madvacanasyāmoghatayā bhāvini janane śarīrāntaraṃ gatāyāḥ asyāḥ sarasijākṣyā rasena ramaṇo bhūtvā muhūrtadvayaṃ maccaraṇayugalabandhakāritayā māsadvayaṃ śṛṅkhalānigaḍitacaraṇo ramaṇīviyogaviṣādamanubhūya paścādanekakālaṃ vallabhayā saha rājyasukhaṃ labhasva'iti // Dkc_1,5.13 //
children.translated_text: Since my words cannot be rendered futile, in a future birth, after this lotus-eyed lady has gone to another body, you shall become her lover by passion, and for a brief time — because you caused the binding of my feet — you shall for two months endure the sorrow of separation from your beloved with your feet bound in chains, and thereafter enjoy the happiness of kingship with your beloved for a long time.' [Dkc 1,5.13]

children.text: START Dkc 1,5.14:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,5.14]

children.text: tadanu jātismaratvamapi tayoranvagṛhṇāt /
"tasmānmarālabandhanaṃ na karaṇīyaṃ tvayā' iti /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, you should not bind the swan.'

children.text: sāpi bhartṛdārikā tadvacanākarṇanābhijñātasvapurātanajananavṛttāntā nūnamayaṃ matprāṇavallabhaḥ' iti manasi jānatī rāgapallavitamānasā samandahāsamavocat--"saumya, purā śāmbo yajñavatīsandeśaparipālanāya tathāvidhaṃ haṃsabandhanamakārṣīt /
children.translated_text: The noble princess too, having recognized the events of her own former life upon hearing his words, knowing in her heart 'surely this is my beloved,' with her mind blossoming with love, spoke with a gentle smile: 'Noble sir, in the past <s>Śāmba</s> performed such a binding of the swan in order to fulfill the message of <s>Yajñavatī</s>.

children.text: tathāhi loke paṇḍitā api dākṣiṇyenākāryaṃ kurvanti' iti /
children.translated_text: For indeed, even wise men in the world do improper things out of gallantry.'

children.text: kanyākumārāvevamanyonyapurātanajanananāmadheye paricite parasparajñānāya sābhijñamuktvā manojarāgapūrṇamānasau babhūvatuḥ // Dkc_1,5.14 //
children.translated_text: The maiden and the youth, having thus made known to each other the names from their former births for the sake of mutual recognition, speaking with full understanding, became filled with love in their hearts. [Dkc 1,5.14]
Thereafter, the memory of past births also took hold of those two.

children.text: START Dkc 1,5.15:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,5.15]

children.text: tasminnavasare mālavendramahiṣī parijanaparivṛtā duhitṛkelīvilokanāya taṃ deśamavāpa /
children.translated_text: At that moment, the chief queen of the king of <s>Mālava</s>, surrounded by her retinue, arrived at that place to watch her daughter at play.

children.text: bālacandrikā tu tāṃ dūrato vilokya sasambhramaṃ rahasyanirbhedabhiyā hastasaṃjñayā puṣpodbhavasevyamānaṃ rājavāhanaṃ vṛkṣavāṭikāntaritagātramakarot /
children.translated_text: <s>Bālacandrikā</s>, seeing her [mistress] from afar, hastily — out of fear that the secret might be discovered — concealed <s>Rājavāhana</s>, who was being attended by <s>Puṣpodbhava</s>, behind the screen of the garden trees.

children.text: sā mānasāramahiṣī sakhīsametāyā duhiturnānāvidhāṃ vihāralīlāmanubhavantī kṣaṇaṃ sthitvā duhitrā sametā nijāgāragamanāyodyuktā babhūva /
children.translated_text: That chief queen of <s>Mānasāra</s>, having enjoyed various kinds of pleasure-pastimes with her daughter who was accompanied by her friends, stayed for a while and then prepared to depart with her daughter to her own palace.

children.text: mātaramanugacchantī avantisundarī rājahaṃsakulatilaka, vihāravāñchayā kelivane madantikamāgataṃ bhavantamakāṇḍe eva visṛjya mayā samucitamiti jananyanugamanaṃ kriyate--tadanena bhavanmanorāgo 'nyathā mā bhūt' iti marālamiva kumāramuddiśya samucitālāpakalāpaṃ vadantī punaḥ punaḥ parivṛttadīnanayanā vadanaṃ vilokayantī nijamandiramagāt // Dkc_1,5.15 //
children.translated_text: <s>Avantisundarī</s>, following her mother, [said:] 'O ornament of the lineage of <s>Rājahaṃsa</s>! You came to my vicinity in the pleasure-grove out of a desire for amusement, and it is fitting that I now leave you so abruptly to follow my mother — may your love for me not become otherwise because of this.' Thus speaking appropriate words of sweet conversation, as if addressing a <s>marāla</s> (royal swan), directed at the prince, glancing back again and again with sorrowful eyes at his face, she went to her own palace. (Dkc 1,5.15)

children.text: START Dkc 1,5.16:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,5.16]

children.text: tatra hṛdayavallabhakathāprasaṅge bālacandrikākathitatadanvayanāmadheyā manmathabāṇapatanavyākulamānasā virahavedanayā dine dine bahulapakṣaśaśikaleva kṣāmakṣāmāhārādisakalaṃ vyāpāraṃ parihṛtya rahasyamandire malayajarasakṣālitapallavakusumakalpitatalpalatāvartitanulatā babhūva // Dkc_1,5.16 //
children.translated_text: There, in the course of conversation about her heart's beloved, her mind agitated by the falling of <s>Manmatha's</s> (<s>Kāmadeva's</s>) arrows — [she] whose family name had been told by <s>Bālacandrikā</s> — tormented by the pain of separation, growing more and more emaciated day by day like the moon in the dark fortnight, having abandoned all activities including eating, in a secret chamber, upon a couch fashioned of sprouts and flowers washed with sandalwood paste, she became a slender creeper entwined upon a bed of vines. (Dkc 1,5.16)

children.text: START Dkc 1,5.17:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,5.17]

children.text:
tatra tathāvidhāvasthāmanubhavantīṃ manmathānalasantaptāṃ sukumārīṃ kumārīṃ nirīkṣya khinno vayasyagaṇaḥ kāñcanakalaśasañcitāni haricandanośīraghanasāramilitāni tadabhiṣekakalpitāni salilāni bisatantumayāni vāsāṃsi ca nalinīdalamayāni tālavṛntāni ca santāpaharaṇāni bahūni saṃpādya tasyāḥ śarīramaśiśirayat /
tadapi śītalopacaraṇaṃ salilamiva taptataile tadaṅgadahanameva samantādāviścakāra /
kiṅkartavyatāmūḍhāṃ viṣaṇṇāṃ bālacandrikāmīṣadunmīlitena kaṭākṣavīkṣitena bāṣpakaṇākulena virahānaloṣṇaniḥśvāsaglapitādharayā natāṅgyā śanaiḥ śanaiḥ sagadgadaṃ vyalāpi-"priyasakhi !' kāmaḥ kusumāyudhaḥ pañcabāṇa iti nūnamasatyamucyate /
iyamahamayomayairasaṃkhyairiṣubhiranena hanye /
sakhi, candramasaṃ vaḍavānalādatitāpakaraṃ manye /
children.translated_text: Friend, I think the moon is more scorching than the submarine fire (<s>vaḍavānala</s>);

children.text: yadasminnantaḥpraviśati śuṣyati pārāvāraḥ, sati nirgate tadaiva vardhate /
children.translated_text: for when it enters [the ocean], the ocean dries up, and when it rises, [the ocean] immediately swells.

children.text: doṣākarasya duṣkarma kiṃ varṇyate mayā /
children.translated_text: What can I say of the evil deeds of the moon (<s>doṣākara</s>, 'maker of faults')?

children.text: yadanena nijasodaryāḥ padmālayāyāḥ gehabhūtamapi kamalaṃ vihanyate // Dkc_1,5.17 //
children.translated_text: For by it, even the lotus — the dwelling of [its] own sister <s>Padmālayā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) — is destroyed. (Dkc 1,5.17)

There, seeing the delicate maiden in such a state, scorched by the fire of <s>Manmatha</s> (the love-god), her group of companions was distressed. Having procured waters collected in golden pots, mixed with yellow sandalwood, <s>uśīra</s> (vetiver), and camphor — prepared for her ablution — garments made of lotus fiber, and many palm-leaf fans to remove the heat, they cooled her body. But even that cooling treatment, like water poured on hot oil, only increased the burning of her limbs on all sides. With a sidelong glance slightly opened, brimming with teardrops, her lower lip withered by the hot sighs of the fire of separation, her body bent low, slowly and falteringly she spoke to <s>Bālacandrikā</s>, who was perplexed about what to do and dejected: 'Dear friend! That <s>Kāma</s> is [called] the flower-weaponed, the five-arrowed one — surely this is falsely said! I am being slain by him with innumerable arrows made of iron!

children.text: START Dkc 1,5.18:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,5.18]

children.text:
virahānalasaṃtaptahṛdayasparśena nūnamuṣṇīkṛtaḥ svalpībhavati malayānilaḥ /
navapallavakalpitaṃ talpamidamanaṅgāgniśikhāpaṭalamiva santāpaṃ tanostanoti /
haricandanamapi purā nijayaṣṭisaṃśleṣavaduragaradanaliptolvaṇagaralasaṃkalitamiva tāpayati śarīram /
tasmādalamalamāyāsena śītalopacāre /
children.translated_text: Therefore, enough, enough of this effort at cooling treatment!

children.text: lāvaṇyajitamāro rājakumāra evāgadaṅkāro manmathajvarāpaharaṇe /
children.translated_text: Only the prince, who conquers <s>Māra</s> (the love-god) in charm, would be the remedy for removing the fever of <s>Manmatha</s>.

children.text: so 'pi labdhumaśakyo mayā /
children.translated_text: But even he is unattainable by me.

children.text: kiṃ karomi' iti // Dkc_1,5.18 //
children.translated_text: What shall I do?' (Dkc 1,5.18)

Surely the <s>Malaya</s> breeze becomes warm and diminishes from the touch of my heart scorched by the fire of separation; this couch fashioned of fresh sprouts spreads [more] heat over my body like a canopy of <s>Anaṅga's</s> (the bodiless love-god's) fire-flames; even yellow sandalwood, as if smeared with the virulent poison of a serpent's fangs through the former embrace of its own trunk, burns my body.

children.text: START Dkc 1,5.19:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,5.19]

children.text:
bālacandrikā manojajvarāvasthāparamakāṣṭhāṃ gatāṃ komalāṅgīṃ tāṃ rājavāhanalāvaṇyādhīnamānasāmananyaśaraṇāmavekṣyātmanyacintayat-- "kumāraḥ satvaramānetavyo mayā /
no cedenāṃ smaraṇīyāṃ gatiṃ neṣyati mīnaketanaḥ /
tatrodyāne kumārayoranyonyāvalokanavelāyāmasamasāyakaḥ samaṃ muktasāyako 'bhūt /
tasmātkumārānayanaṃ sukaram' iti /
tato 'vantisundarīrakṣaṇāya samayocitakaraṇīyacaturaṃ sakhīgaṇaṃ niyujya rājakumāramandiramavāpa /
children.translated_text: Then, entrusting to the group of friends — who were skilled in doing what was appropriate for the occasion — the protection of <s>Avantisundarī</s>, she went to the prince's residence.

children.text: puṣpabāṇabāṇatūṇīrāyamānamānaso 'naṅgataptāvayavasaṃparkaparimlānapallavaśayanamadhiṣṭhito rājavāhanaḥ prāṇeśvarīmuddiśya saha puṣpodbhavena saṃlapannāgatāṃ priyavayasyāmālokya pādamūlamanveṣaṇīyā lateva bālacandrikāgateti saṃtuṣṭamanā niṭilataṭamaṇṅanībhavadambujakorakākṛtilasadañjalipuṭām "ito niṣīda' iti nirdiṣṭasamucitāsanāsīnāmavantisundarīpreṣitaṃ sakarpūraṃ tāmbūlaṃ vinayena dadatīṃ tāṃ kāntāvṛttāntamapṛcchat /
children.translated_text: <s>Rājavāhana</s>, whose mind had become a quiver for <s>Puṣpabāṇa's</s> (<s>Kāmadeva's</s>) arrows, reclining on a bed of sprouts wilted from contact with limbs scorched by <s>Anaṅga</s> (the bodiless love-god), conversing with <s>Puṣpodbhava</s> about the lady of his life — seeing his dear friend arrive, his mind delighted, [thinking] '<s>Bālacandrikā</s> has come — [she is] like a creeper to be sought at the foot [of a tree]!' — [he] directed her to a suitable seat, [saying] 'Sit here,' to her whose joined palms formed the shape of a lotus bud at the front of her forehead, and as she respectfully offered <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel) with camphor, sent by <s>Avantisundarī</s>, he asked her about the news of his beloved.

children.text: tayā savinayamabhāṇi-"deva, krīḍāvane bhavadavalokanakālamārabhya manmathamathyamānā puṣpatalpādiṣu tāpaśamanamalabhamānā vāmanenevonnatataruphalamalabhyaṃ tvaduraḥ sthalāliṅganasaukhyaṃ smarāndhatayā lipsuḥ sā svayameva patrikāmālikhya "vallabhāyaināmarpaya' iti māṃ niyuktavatī' /
children.translated_text: She spoke respectfully: 'Lord, from the moment of beholding you in the pleasure-garden, churned by <s>Manmatha</s>, finding no relief from the heat on couches of flowers and the like, as one of short stature [cannot reach] the fruit of a tall tree, longing in her blindness of love to attain the happiness of embracing your chest — which is unattainable — she herself wrote a letter and, [saying] "deliver this to my beloved," dispatched me.'

children.text: rājakumāraḥ patrikāṃ tāmādāya papāṭha- // Dkc_1,5.19 //
children.translated_text: The prince, taking that letter, read it: (Dkc 1,5.19)

<s>Bālacandrikā</s>, seeing the delicate-limbed one who had reached the extreme limit of the fever of the love-god, whose mind was dependent on the charm of <s>Rājavāhana</s>, and who had no other refuge, thought to herself: 'The prince must be brought quickly by me; otherwise, the flower-bannered one (<s>Kāmadeva</s>) will lead this one who is worthy of remembrance to [her] end. In that garden, at the moment when the two [young people] beheld each other, the unequal-arrowed one (<s>Kāma</s>) released his arrows equally [at both]. Therefore, bringing the prince will be easy.'

children.text: START Dkc 1,5.20:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,5.20]

children.text: `subhaga kusumasukumāraṃ jagadanavadyaṃ vilokya te rūpam /
children.translated_text: 'O handsome one, having beheld your form, delicate as a flower and faultless in the world,

children.text: mama mānasamabhilaṣati tvaṃ cittaṃ kuru tathā mṛdulam' // Dkc_1,5.20 //
children.translated_text: my heart desires you — therefore make your mind equally tender.' (Dkc 1,5.20)

children.text: START Dkc 1,5.21:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,5.21]

children.text:
iti paṭhitvā sādaramabhāṣata-"sakhi, chāyāvanmāmanuvartamānasya puṣpodbhavasya vallabhā tvameva tasyā mṛgīdṛśo bahiścarāḥ prāṇā iva vartase /
tvaccāturyamasyāṃ kriyālatāyāmālavālamabhūt /
yattavābhīṣṭaṃ yena priyāmanorathaḥ phaliṣyati tadakhilaṃ kariṣyāmi /
natāṅgyā manmanaḥ kāṭhinyamākhyātam /
yadā kelivane kuraṅgalocanā locanapathamavartata tadaiṣāpahṛtamadīyamānasā sā svamandiramagāt /
sā cetaso mādhuryakāṭhinye svayameva jānāti /
children.translated_text: She herself knows the sweetness and hardness of [my] heart.

children.text: duṣkaraḥ kanyāntaḥpurapraveśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Entry into the inner apartments of a maiden is difficult.

children.text: tadanurūpamupāyamupapādya śvaḥ paraśvo vā matāṅgīṃ saṅgamiṣyāmi /
children.translated_text: Therefore, devising a suitable stratagem, tomorrow or the day after, I shall meet the elephant-gaited one.

children.text: madudantamevamākhyāya śirīṣakusumasukumārāyā yathā śarīrabādhā na jāyeta tathāvidhamupāyamācara' iti // Dkc_1,5.21 //
children.translated_text: Convey this message of mine to her, and employ such means that no bodily affliction may arise for [her who is] delicate as a <s>śirīṣa</s> flower.' (Dkc 1,5.21)

Having read this, he spoke affectionately: 'Friend, you who follow <s>Puṣpodbhava</s> (<s>Kāmadeva</s>) like a shadow are indeed his beloved, and you are like the external life-breaths of that doe-eyed one. Your cleverness has been the support-rope for this creeper of action. Whatever is your desire, by which the heart's wish of my beloved will bear fruit — all that I shall do. Through your bowed form, the hardness of my mind has been revealed. When the fawn-eyed one entered the path of my eyes in the pleasure-garden, she who had stolen my mind went to her own palace.

children.text: START Dkc 1,5.22:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,5.22]

children.text: bālacandrikāpi tasya premagarbhitaṃ vacanamākarṇya saṃtuṣṭā kanyāpuramagacchat /
children.translated_text: <s>Bālacandrikā</s>, hearing his words pregnant with love, was delighted and went to the maiden's quarters.

children.text: rājavāhano 'pi yatra hṛdayavallabhāvalokanasukhamalabhata tadudyānaṃ virahavinodāya puṣpodbhavasamanvito jagāma /
children.translated_text: <s>Rājavāhana</s> too went to the garden where he had obtained the happiness of beholding his heart's beloved, accompanied by <s>Puṣpodbhava</s>, to divert [himself from] the pain of separation.

children.text: tatra cakoralocanāvacitapallavakusumanikurambaṃ mahīruhasamūhaṃ śaradindumukhyā manmathasamārādhanasthānaṃ ca natāṅgīpadapaṅkticihnitaṃ śītalasaikatatalaṃ ca sudatībhuktamuktaṃ mādhavīlatāmaṇḍapāntarapallavatalpaṃ ca vilokayaṃllalanātilakavilokanavelājanitaśeṣāṇi smāraṃsmāraṃ mandamārutakampitāni navacūtapallavāni madanāgniśikhā iva cakito darśandarśaṃ manojakarṇejapānāmiva kokilakīramadhukarāṇāṃ kvaṇitāni śrāvaṃ śrāvaṃ māravikāreṇa kvacidapyavasthātumasahiṣṇuḥ paribabhrāma // Dkc_1,5.22 //
children.translated_text: There, seeing the clusters of trees with sprouts and flowers gathered by the <s>cakora</s>-eyed one, and the place of worship of <s>Manmatha</s> with its autumn-moon-[like] face, and the cool sandy bank marked by the rows of the bent-bodied one's footprints, and the couch of sprouts within the bower of <s>mādhavī</s> creepers that had been enjoyed and then left by the beautiful lady — remembering each [scene] from the moment of beholding the crest-jewel among women, startled again and again at the sight of the tender mango sprouts trembling in the gentle breeze like the flame-tips of <s>Manmatha's</s> fire, and hearing again and again the calls of cuckoos, parrots, and bees that were like whispers in the ear of the love-god — unable to remain in any one place due to the agitation of love, he wandered about. (Dkc 1,5.22)

children.text: START Dkc 1,5.23:
children.translated_text: [Start of Dkc 1,5.23]

children.text:
tasminnavasare dharaṇīsura ekaḥ sūkṣmacitranivasanaṃ sphuranmaṇikuṇḍalamaṇḍito muṇḍitamastakamānavasametaścaturaveśamanoramo yadṛcchayā samāgataḥ samantato 'bhyullasattejomaṇḍalaṃ rājavāhanamāśīrvādapūrvakaṃ dadarśa /
rājavāhanaḥ sādaram ko bhavān, kasyāṃ vidyāyāṃ nipuṇaḥ' iti taṃ papraccha /
sa ca "vidyeśvaranāmadheyo 'hamaindrajālikavidyākovido vividhadeśeṣu rājamanorañjanāya bhramannujjayinīmadyāgato 'smi' iti śaśaṃsa /
punarapi rājavāhanaṃ samyagālokya "asyāṃ līlāvanau pāṇḍuratānimittaṃ kim' iti sābhiprāyaṃ vihasyāpṛcchat /
puṣpodbhavaśca nijakāryakaraṇaṃ tarkayannenamādareṇa babhāṣe-"nanu satāṃ sakhyasyābhāṣaṇapūrvatayā ciraṃ rucirabhāṣaṇo bhavānasmākaṃ priyavayasyo jātaḥ /
suhṛdāmakathyaṃ ca kimasti? kelivane 'sminvasantamahotsavāyāgatāyā mālavendrasutāyā rājanandanasyāsya cākasmikadarśane 'nyonyānuragātirekaḥ samajāyata /
satatasaṃbhogasiddhyapāyābhāvenāsāvīdṛśīmavasthāmanubhavati iti /
children.translated_text: Because there is no means to achieve constant union, she is experiencing such a [pitiable] state.

children.text: vidyeśvaro lajjābhirāmaṃ rājakumāramukhamabhivīkṣya viracitamandahāso vyājahāra-"deva !bhavadanucare mayi tiṣṭhati tava kāryamasādhyaṃ kimasti /
children.translated_text: <s>Vidyeśvara</s>, gazing upon the charmingly bashful face of the prince, broke into a gentle smile and said: 'My lord! With me, your servant, at hand, what task of yours is impossible to accomplish?

children.text: ahamindrajālavidyayā mālavendraṃ mohayan paurajanasamakṣameva tattanayāpariṇayaṃ racayitvā kanyāntaḥpurapraveśaṃ kārayiṣyāmīti vṛttānta eṣa rājakanyakāyai sakhīmukhena pūrvameva kathayitavyaḥ' iti /
children.translated_text: I, by my mastery of the <s>indrajāla</s> (magic illusion) art, shall bewilder the lord of <s>Mālava</s> and, before the very eyes of the townsfolk, arrange the marriage with his daughter and effect [the prince's] entry into the women's quarters of the princess — but this plan must first be communicated to the princess through the mouth of a confidante.'

children.text: saṃtuṣṭamanā mahīpatiranimittaṃ mitraṃ prakaṭīkṛtakṛtrimakriyāpāṭavaṃ vipralambhakṛtrimapremasahajasauhārdavedinaṃ taṃ vidyeśvaraṃ sabahumānaṃ visasarja // Dkc_1,5.23 //
children.translated_text: The prince, his mind delighted, reverently dismissed <s>Vidyeśvara</s> — a friend [acquired] without cause, who had displayed his dexterity in contrived arts, and who, though his affection was a contrivance born of deception, knew the genuine goodwill [behind it].
