children.translated_text: Thus settled, all the princes headed by <s>Rājavāhana</s>, governing the entire circle of the earth justly by <s>Rājavāhana</s>'s command, maintaining mutual unanimity, enjoyed royal pleasures that are exceedingly difficult to obtain even for <s>Purandara</s> (Indra) and the other gods.

Thus ends the eighth <s>ucchvāsa</s> (chapter) named the adventures of <s>Viśruta</s> in the <s>Daśakumāracarita</s> (The Tale of the Ten Princes) composed by <s>Śrī Daṇḍin</s>. 8. Now, the <s>kathopasaṃhāra</s> (narrative conclusion).
Then those princes who had gathered there — <s>Apahāravarman</s>, <s>Upahāravarman</s>, <s>Arthapāla</s>, <s>Pramati</s>, <s>Mitragupta</s>, <s>Mantragupta</s>, and <s>Viśruta</s> — summoned through servants the prince <s>Somadatta</s>, who was enjoying the position of heir-apparent in <s>Pāṭalipura</s>, together with his wife <s>Vāmalocanā</s>, in accordance with a previously arranged signal. And all of them, together with <s>Rājavāhana</s>, having assembled and being filled with mutual delight, were exchanging stories when royal messengers arrived bearing a letter of command from King <s>Rājahaṃsa</s> of <s>Puṣpapura</s>. Bowing to <s>Rājavāhana</s>, they announced — "Lord, please accept this letter of command from your father, King <s>Rājahaṃsa</s>." Hearing this, he rose and bowed again and again with respect, and in the assembly accepted that letter of command.
Placing it upon his head, then opening and unsealing it, King <s>Rājavāhana</s> had it read aloud for all to hear — "Hail and prosperity! From the royal capital of <s>Puṣpapura</s>, the illustrious King <s>Rājahaṃsa</s> sends this letter of command, instructing the princes headed by <s>Rājavāhana</s> residing in the city of <s>Campā</s>.
As follows: After you took leave of me, bowed, and departed, on the road at a certain forest tract, you encamped near a temple of <s>Śiva</s>.
There, when <s>Rājavāhana</s>, who had stayed in the <s>Śiva</s> temple at night for the purpose of worshipping <s>Śiva</s>, was not found in the morning, all the remaining princes, vowing 'We shall bow before <s>Rājahaṃsa</s> together with <s>Rājavāhana</s> or else we shall give up our lives,' turned the army back and set out separately to search for <s>Rājavāhana</s>.
Hearing this account of your circumstances from the mouths of the soldiers who had returned, both of us — I and your mother — our minds sunk in an ocean of unbearable grief, resolved 'Let us go to the hermitage of <s>Vāmadeva</s>, make this matter known to him, and give up our lives.' Having gone to that hermitage and bowed to that sage, just as we stood there, that sage who knows the three times already knew our intention.
Understanding our resolve, he spoke — 'O King, all this, your intention, was already known to me through the power of insight.
But your princes, on account of <s>Rājavāhana</s>, having encountered considerable hardship, by the rising of their fortune, with extraordinary valor, having accomplished conquest of the directions, having obtained many kingdoms, at the end of sixteen years, placing the victorious <s>Rājavāhana</s> at their head, will return and bow at your feet and those of <s>Vasumatī</s>, and will be obedient to your commands.
Therefore, no rash act should be undertaken on their account.'
Hearing that, relying on faith in his words, from that day onward I and the queen have sustained our lives.
Now, as the appointed time draws near, we went to the hermitage of <s>Vāmadeva</s> and made a petition — 'Lord, the time limit you stated is nearly fulfilled; is their news known to you even now?'
Hearing this, the sage said — 'O King, all the princes headed by <s>Rājavāhana</s>, having defeated many unconquerable enemies, having accomplished the conquest of the directions, having brought the circle of the earth under their sway, are stationed together in <s>Campā</s>.
Send servants quickly, bearing your letter of command, to bring them.'
Hearing the sage's words, this letter of command has been dispatched for your summoning.
Hereafter, if you delay even a moment, then know that you will hear of me and your mother <s>Vasumatī</s> only as a tale of the past — therefore, even water should be drunk on the road without stopping."
Thus, placing the father's letter of command upon his head, they resolved, "Let us go."
Then, having appointed capable and trusted men with sufficient armies to guard the conquered kingdoms at every place, and arranging road-protection with a limited force, they first defeated <s>Mānasāra</s>, the lord of <s>Mālava</s>, bringing that kingdom too under their control, and proceeded to bow at the feet of King <s>Rājahaṃsa</s> and Queen <s>Vasumatī</s> in <s>Puṣpapura</s>.
Having resolved thus, accompanied by their respective wives, they set out with a limited army against the lord of <s>Mālava</s>.
Reaching <s>Ujjayinī</s>, with the help of those allied princes, even <s>Mānasāra</s>, the lord of <s>Mālava</s>, though exceedingly powerful, was defeated and slain in a moment by <s>Rājavāhana</s> with his limited force.
Then, taking his daughter <s>Avantisundarī</s>, and liberating prince <s>Puṣpodbhava</s> along with his family, who had previously been imprisoned by <s>Caṇḍavarman</s>, that minister, they brought them along, brought the kingdom of the lord of <s>Mālava</s> under control, appointed some ministers with armies for its protection, and the princes with their remaining limited forces reached <s>Puṣpapura</s>. Placing <s>Rājavāhana</s> at their head, they bowed at the feet of King <s>Rājahaṃsa</s> and mother <s>Vasumatī</s>.
And those two, having attained the reunion with their sons, reached supreme bliss.
Then, in the presence of the king and Queen <s>Vasumatī</s>,
<s>Vāmadeva</s>, having ascertained the wishes of all ten princes headed by <s>Rājavāhana</s>, commanded them — 'All of you, going at once, should govern your respective kingdoms justly.
And whenever you wish, you should come to pay respects at the feet of your parents.'
Then all the princes, placing the sage's words upon their heads and bowing to him and to their parents, narrated their respective adventures from the conquest of the directions until their return, each separately, in the presence of the sage.
And the parents, hearing the extremely difficult exploits demonstrating the valor of the princes, attained supreme bliss.
Then the king respectfully addressed the sage — 'Blessed one, by your grace we have attained happiness that surpasses human desires and is beyond the reach of speech and mind.
Henceforth, it is proper for me to adopt the <s>vānaprastha</s> (forest-dweller) stage of life in your holy presence and devote myself to spiritual practice.
Therefore, having consecrated <s>Rājavāhana</s> as king over the kingdom of <s>Puṣpapura</s> and the kingdom of <s>Mānasāra</s>, and having duly distributed the remaining kingdoms to the nine princes, let those princes, obedient to <s>Rājavāhana</s>'s commands, acting in unanimity, uproot all thorns from the earth girdled by the four oceans and enjoy it — may the lord so ordain.'
When the sage observed great insistence from the princes in opposing their father's intention to adopt the <s>vānaprastha</s> (forest-dweller) stage, he addressed them — 'O princes, this your father, proceeding on the path appropriate to his age, without bodily hardship, stationed at my hermitage, should by no means be prevented from embracing the <s>vānaprastha</s> (forest-dweller) stage of life.

children.text: iti śrīdaṇḍinaḥ kṛtau daśakumāracarite kathopasaṃhāraḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>kathopasaṃhāra</s> (narrative conclusion) in the <s>Daśakumāracarita</s> (The Tale of the Ten Princes) composed by <s>Śrī Daṇḍin</s>.

children.text: iti śrīmahāmahopādhyāyakavikulasārvabhaumanikhilavidyākumudinīśarvarīśvarasarasvatīniḥśvasitakaṣidaṇḍipaṇḍitaviracitaṃ daśakumāracaritaṃ saṃpūrṇam
children.translated_text: Thus concludes the <s>Daśakumāracarita</s> (Tale of the Ten Princes), composed by the illustrious <s>Daṇḍin</s>, the great teacher of teachers, the sovereign of all poet-clans, the lord of the night of the night-lotus (<s>kumud</s>) of all branches of learning, the breath of <s>Sarasvatī</s> herself.
